The **[2010–11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_NHL_season "2010–11 NHL season")[Vancouver Canucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Canucks "Vancouver Canucks") season** was the 41st season in the modern Canucks history. The [Vancouver Canucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Canucks "Vancouver Canucks") won their fifth [Northwest division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Division_(NHL) "Northwest Division (NHL)") title, third conference championship and first [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-3) They also reached the [Stanley Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup_Final "Stanley Cup Final") for the third time in franchise history, losing to the [Boston Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Bruins "Boston Bruins") in seven games. This marked the last time a Canadian team contended in the Stanley Cup Final until the [Montreal Canadiens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal_Canadiens "Montreal Canadiens") did so in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Stanley_Cup_Final "2021 Stanley Cup Final"), ten years later.

As of the [2025-26 NHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025-26_NHL_season "2025-26 NHL season"), this is the most recent Presidents’ Trophy winner to reach the Finals in a full 82-game season.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Off-season")]

#### Entry draft

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Entry draft")]

The [2010 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NHL_entry_draft "2010 NHL entry draft") was held June 25–26, 2010, at [Staples Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), California. The Canucks had the 25th overall draft choice in the first round as a result of being defeated by the [Chicago Blackhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks") in the [Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_(NHL) "Western Conference (NHL)") semi-final, but that draft choice was traded to the [Florida Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Panthers "Florida Panthers"). The Canucks also did not have a second- or third-round draft pick. Their second-round pick was traded to the [Buffalo Sabres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Sabres "Buffalo Sabres") in exchange for [Steve Bernier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Bernier "Steve Bernier").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-4) Their third-round pick was traded to the [Carolina Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Hurricanes "Carolina Hurricanes") at the NHL trade deadline in exchange for [Andrew Alberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Alberts "Andrew Alberts").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-5) The Canucks acquired an additional sixth-round draft choice from the [Phoenix Coyotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Coyotes "Arizona Coyotes") as a result of a trade that sent [Mathieu Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathieu_Schneider "Mathieu Schneider") to Phoenix.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-mschneider-6) Vancouver had the 115th, 145th, 172nd, 175th and 205th overall draft choices.

#### Trades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Trades")]

On June 25, 2010, the Canucks acquired [Keith Ballard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Ballard "Keith Ballard") and [Victor Oreskovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Oreskovich "Victor Oreskovich") from the [Florida Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Panthers "Florida Panthers") in exchange for [Steve Bernier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Bernier "Steve Bernier"), [Michael Grabner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Grabner "Michael Grabner") and the 25th overall pick in the 2010 NHL Entry Draft.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-ballard-7)

Mike Gillis traded [Shane O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_O'Brien_(ice_hockey) "Shane O'Brien (ice hockey)") and Dan Gendur to the [Nashville Predators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Predators "Nashville Predators") in exchange for [Ryan Parent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Parent "Ryan Parent") and [Jonas Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Andersson_(ice_hockey) "Jonas Andersson (ice hockey)") on October 5, 2010. Parent was immediately waived after being acquired while Andersson was assigned to the [Manitoba Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba_Moose "Manitoba Moose") (now St. John's Ice Caps) of the [American Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-obtrade-8) On October 6, [Darcy Hordichuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darcy_Hordichuk "Darcy Hordichuk") was traded to the Florida Panthers in exchange for [Andrew Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Peters "Andrew Peters"). Peters would play for the Manitoba Moose.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-apeters-9)

On October 7, Mike Gillis made another trade with the Florida Panthers, this time acquiring [Nathan Paetsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Paetsch "Nathan Paetsch") for [Sean Zimmerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Zimmerman "Sean Zimmerman").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-npaetsch-10)

#### Player signings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Player signings")]

On April 6, 2010, the Canucks signed Swedish [goaltender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goaltender "Goaltender")[Eddie Läck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_L%C3%A4ck "Eddie Läck") to a two-year entry-level contract.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-lack-11) Lack spent the 2009–10 season as a member of the [Brynäs IF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryn%C3%A4s_IF "Brynäs IF"), posting a 2.67 [goals against average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goals_against_average "Goals against average") (GAA) and a .911 [save percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_percentage "Save percentage"). He was expected to start the year with the Manitoba Moose.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-12)

On May 31, 2010, the Canucks announced that they signed three defencemen, including prospect [Yann Sauvé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yann_Sauv%C3%A9 "Yann Sauvé"). Sauvé was drafted 41st overall by the Canucks in the [2008 draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NHL_Entry_Draft "2008 NHL Entry Draft"). In addition, they signed free agent [Lee Sweatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Sweatt "Lee Sweatt") and [Christopher Tanev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Tanev "Christopher Tanev"). Sweatt split time in the Finnish [SM-liiga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liiga "Liiga") and [Kontinental Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kontinental_Hockey_League "Kontinental Hockey League") (KHL) for the 2009–10 season. He registered nine goals and seven assists in 21 games for [TPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TPS_(ice_hockey) "TPS (ice hockey)") in Finland. Sweatt added two goals and five assists in 37 games in the KHL with [Dinamo Riga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinamo_Riga "Dinamo Riga"). Christopher Tanev signed as a free agent after playing in the [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Hockey "Atlantic Hockey"), where he scored 10 goals and 18 assists in 41 games for the [RIT Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIT_Tigers_men's_ice_hockey "RIT Tigers men's ice hockey").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-3d-13)

On June 1, 2010, Vancouver signed [Anton Rödin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_R%C3%B6din "Anton Rödin") to a three-year, entry-level contract. Rödin was drafted 53rd overall by the Canucks in the [2009 Draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NHL_Entry_Draft "2009 NHL Entry Draft"). He spent the 2009–10 season in the [Swedish Elite League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Hockey_League "Swedish Hockey League") with Brynäs IF. He also played at the [2010 World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_World_Junior_Ice_Hockey_Championships "2010 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships"), where he won a bronze medal with Sweden. He finished the tournament tied for second in scoring for Sweden with three goals and ten points, good enough for ninth in the tournament.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-14)

On June 2, 2010, Mike Gillis signed [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider") to a contract extension with the team. He was drafted in the first round, 26th overall, of the [2004 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NHL_entry_draft "2004 NHL entry draft") by the Canucks. He spent the last two seasons playing with the [Manitoba Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba_Moose "Manitoba Moose") of the AHL, where he was named the League's [Goaltender of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldege_%22Baz%22_Bastien_Memorial_Award "Aldege \"Baz\" Bastien Memorial Award") in [2008–09](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_AHL_season "2008–09 AHL season") while leading the Moose to the [Calder Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Calder_Cup_Playoffs "2009 Calder Cup Playoffs").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-cschneider-15) The Canucks also announced that they signed [Peter Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Andersson_(ice_hockey_b._1991) "Peter Andersson (ice hockey b. 1991)") to an entry-level contract. Andersson was drafted 143rd overall by the Canucks in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NHL_Entry_Draft "2009 NHL Entry Draft").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-16)

On June 16, 2010, the Vancouver Canucks re-signed pending unrestricted free agent [Aaron Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rome "Aaron Rome") to a two-year contract. The deal is worth $1.5 million and will have a [salary cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL_Salary_Cap "NHL Salary Cap") hit of $750,000 per season.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-arome-17) On July 2, 2010, [Alexandre Bolduc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Bolduc "Alexandre Bolduc") signed a one-year, two-way contract worth $500,000.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-bolduc-18)[Shane O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_O'Brien_(ice_hockey) "Shane O'Brien (ice hockey)") re-signed with the Canucks on July 6, 2010, when he accepted his qualifying offer. The new contract will pay O'Brien $1.6 million for one year.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-sob-19)[Tanner Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanner_Glass "Tanner Glass") also signed a one-year contract worth $625,000.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-tglass-20)

On July 22, [Jannik Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jannik_Hansen "Jannik Hansen") was awarded a one-year contract worth $825,000 by an arbitrator.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-jhansen-21)

On July 26, the Canucks re-signed [Mason Raymond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Raymond "Mason Raymond") to a new two-year contract worth a total of $5.1 million.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-mraymond-22)

#### Free agency

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Free agency")]

On July 1, the Vancouver Canucks signed [Dan Hamhuis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Hamhuis "Dan Hamhuis") to a six-year contract worth $27 million,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-hamhuis-23)[Jeff Tambellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Tambellini "Jeff Tambellini") to a 1-year contract worth $500,000,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-jtambellini-24)[Manny Malhotra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manny_Malhotra "Manny Malhotra") to a three-year contract worth $7.5 million and [Joel Perrault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Perrault "Joel Perrault") to a one-year contract worth $510,000.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-july1-25) The Canucks signed [Tyler Weiman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Weiman "Tyler Weiman") on July 12 to a one-year contract worth $500,000.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-tweiman-26)

The Canucks signed unrestricted free agent [Raffi Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffi_Torres "Raffi Torres") to a one-year contract worth $1 million on August 25.

On October 7, the Canucks signed [Peter Schaefer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Schaefer_(ice_hockey) "Peter Schaefer (ice hockey)") to a one-year, two-way contract worth $600,000. Schaefer played for the Canucks between 1998 and 2000 before being traded to the [Ottawa Senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa_Senators "Ottawa Senators") for [Sami Salo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Salo "Sami Salo").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-pschaefer-28)

### Pre-season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Pre-season")]

#### Training camp

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Training camp")]

The Canucks held their training camp in [Penticton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penticton "Penticton"), British Columbia, at the [South Okanagan Events Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Okanagan_Events_Centre "South Okanagan Events Centre"). In addition to training camp, the Canucks hosted a Young Stars prospect tournament prior to the start of training camp from September 12 to 16. The event featured prospects from five teams in an eight-game round robin format. The tournament included the [Anaheim Ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim_Ducks "Anaheim Ducks"), [Calgary Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Flames "Calgary Flames"), [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton_Oilers "Edmonton Oilers") and [San Jose Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose_Sharks "San Jose Sharks"). The Canucks finished the tournament with a record of 2–2.

Shortly before the start of training camp, [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo") announced that he would be relinquishing his captaincy. Luongo served as the team captain for two seasons.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-luongocpt-29) Forward [Henrik Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin"), was named team captain.

#### Schedule

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Schedule")]

The Canucks' pre-season schedule began on September 21 against the Calgary Flames. It will be a split series where each franchise will split into two squads to play two simultaneous games, one at the [Saddledome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pengrowth_Saddledome "Pengrowth Saddledome") in Calgary and one at [Rogers Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Arena "Rogers Arena") in Vancouver.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-split-30) In addition, the Canucks will play each of the Edmonton Oilers, Anaheim Ducks and San Jose Sharks twice, once at home and once on the road.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-31) The Canucks finished the preseason with a record of 3–5.

### Regular season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Regular season")]

#### Schedule

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Schedule")]

The Canucks officially kicked off their 2010–11 campaign on October 9 at Rogers Arena against the [Los Angeles Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Kings "Los Angeles Kings"). With the Canucks celebrating their 40th anniversary, the NHL scheduled this game to honour the Canucks' first-ever NHL game against the Los Angeles Kings on October 9, 1970. The Canucks lost the game in a shootout by a score of 2–1. They began the season slowly, going 2–3–1 in their first six games before going on a six-game winning streak. The loss to break the streak came as part of a five-game road trip where they recorded a 2–2–1 record before returning home for their most lopsided loss of the year, a 7–1 defeat at the hands of the [Chicago Blackhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks"). Following the loss the Canucks went 18–4–3, which included an eight-game winning streak, and two four-game winning streaks, before losing three consecutive games in extra time. They proceeded to win the next six games, but ended February alternating wins and losses. Vancouver's win against the [Minnesota Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Wild "Minnesota Wild") on March 14, 2011, put the team at 101 points in the standings. It was the fastest the Canucks reached the 100-point mark in franchise history.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-33) Next, the team recorded its 50th victory of the season for the first time in franchise history on March 27.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-34) They would get top seed in the Western Conference on 2 days later.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-35) And it would get its first [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") two days later.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-36) The season finale took place on April 9, 2011, against the Calgary Flames, which saw the Canucks win 3–2 in overtime. Daniel Sedin registered two assists in order to clinch the [Art Ross Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Ross_Trophy "Art Ross Trophy"), a year after his brother did it.

Excluding four shootout-winning goals, the Canucks scored 258 goals, the most in the League. Furthermore, excluding their five shootout goals allowed, the Canucks gave up only 180 goals in their 82 games, the fewest in the League. They also scored the most power-play goals, with 72, and had the best power-play percentage, at 24.32% (72 for 296).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-38)

The Canucks were also the first team since the [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Stanley_Cup_Final "1978 Stanley Cup Final") champion [Montreal Canadiens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977%E2%80%9378_Montreal_Canadiens_season "1977–78 Montreal Canadiens season") to finish the league with the most goals scored and fewest goals against. They also finished the regular season with the top ranked power play and third ranked penalty kill. They almost finished the same identical record as the [1988–89 Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988%E2%80%9389_Calgary_Flames_season "1988–89 Calgary Flames season") (except they had two fewer losses).

#### Special events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Special events")]

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Orland_Kurtenbach_ring_of_honour.jpg/330px-Orland_Kurtenbach_ring_of_honour.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Orland_Kurtenbach_ring_of_honour.jpg)

[Orland Kurtenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orland_Kurtenbach "Orland Kurtenbach")'s plaque on the Canucks' Ring of Honour in Rogers Arena.

The Canucks kicked off their season with a [pre-game ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-game_ceremony "Pre-game ceremony") on October 9, 2010, to commemorate their 40th Anniversary. They also announced Henrik Sedin as the 13th captain of the team.

Prior to their game on December 11, 2010, against the [Tampa Bay Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Lightning "Tampa Bay Lightning"), the Canucks honoured [Markus Näslund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_N%C3%A4slund "Markus Näslund") by retiring his number 19 jersey. Näslund was the third player in franchise history to receive the honour following [Stan Smyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Smyl "Stan Smyl") and [Trevor Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Linden "Trevor Linden"). Näslund spent 12 seasons with the Canucks, nine as captain. He also holds the franchise lead in points scored with 756. The retirement ceremony coincided with [Mattias Öhlund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattias_%C3%96hlund "Mattias Öhlund")'s return to Vancouver for the first time since signing with the Lightning in 2009.

The Canucks also announced that they will be introducing a "Ring of Honour" to commemorate past players. Four players will have their names added to the ring this season. The first player to get the honour will be [Orland Kurtenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orland_Kurtenbach "Orland Kurtenbach") who was the first ever captain of the Vancouver Canucks. Kurtenbach's ceremony took place on October 26. [Kirk McLean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirk_McLean "Kirk McLean") was added to the ring of honour on November 24. McLean helped lead the Canucks to game seven of the [1994 Stanley Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Stanley_Cup_Final "1994 Stanley Cup Final"). The third player to be inducted into the Ring of Honour will be [Thomas Gradin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Gradin "Thomas Gradin") on January 24. Gradin was part of the 1982 Canucks team that made it to the Stanley Cup Final. He now works as a European scout for organization and is heavily praised at having convinced then-general manager [Dave Nonis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Nonis "Dave Nonis") to draft [Alexander Edler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Edler "Alexander Edler").

The final ceremony took place on March 14 when [Harold Snepsts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Snepsts "Harold Snepsts") was inducted into the Ring of Honour.

### Playoffs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Playoffs")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Henrik_Sedin_accepts_the_trophy.jpg/250px-Henrik_Sedin_accepts_the_trophy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Henrik_Sedin_accepts_the_trophy.jpg)

[Henrik Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin") accepts the [Clarence S. Campbell Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_S._Campbell_Bowl "Clarence S. Campbell Bowl") after the Vancouver Canucks beat the San Jose Sharks to win the Western Conference finals

The Vancouver Canucks were the first team in the NHL to clinch a berth in the playoffs. Two weeks later, they clinched their division on March 16.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-39) The win earned them their fourth [Northwest Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Division_(NHL) "Northwest Division (NHL)") title in five years, thus guaranteeing them home ice advantage in the first round of the [Stanley Cup playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Stanley_Cup_playoffs "2011 Stanley Cup playoffs"). This was the fastest the team had clinched a playoff spot in franchise history.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-playoffsclinch-40) The team earned the top seed in the Western Conference on March 29 and the [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") two days later, guaranteeing home ice advantage throughout the playoffs.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-41)

The Canucks opened their post-season schedule with a series against the eighth-seeded and defending [Stanley Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup "Stanley Cup") champion [Chicago Blackhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-42) This was the third time the two teams played in the playoffs in consecutive years with the Blackhawks winning the first two, both in the second round in six games.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-43) Vancouver won the opening three games of the series before Chicago responded by winning the next three games to force a game seven. [Alexandre Burrows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Burrows "Alexandre Burrows") scored the winning goal in game 7 in overtime on Blackhawks' goaltender [Corey Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Crawford "Corey Crawford") to clinch the 2–1 victory in the game and 4–3 series victory.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-44)

Vancouver moved on to play the fifth-seeded [Nashville Predators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Predators "Nashville Predators") in the second round of the playoffs. It is the first time the two teams had met in the playoffs.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-45) Vancouver won the first game before Nashville won game two to even up the series at one.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-46) Vancouver won both games in Nashville, Game 3 3–2 in overtime on a [Ryan Kesler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Kesler "Ryan Kesler") deflection goal and 4–2 in Game 4, respectively.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-47) The series returned to Vancouver for Game 5 with the Canucks having a 3–1 series lead, where the Predators staved off elimination by beating the Canucks 4–3 and Predators' forward [Joel Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Ward_(ice_hockey) "Joel Ward (ice hockey)") scored two goals, including the game winner to force a game six. The Canucks won the series 4–2 after a 2–1 victory in Game 6 in Nashville to clinch their first Western Conference Final appearance since 1994.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-48)

The Canucks played the second-seeded [San Jose Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose_Sharks "San Jose Sharks") for the first time ever in the [Western Conference Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_(NHL) "Western Conference (NHL)") after San Jose eliminated the third-seeded [Detroit Red Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Red_Wings "Detroit Red Wings") in Game 7. Vancouver prevailed in five games with a double overtime goal scored by defenceman [Kevin Bieksa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Bieksa "Kevin Bieksa") in Game 5 in Vancouver to send the Canucks to the [Stanley Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup_Final "Stanley Cup Final") for the third time in franchise history and the first time since 1994.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-49)

They would face the third-seeded [Boston Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Bruins "Boston Bruins") after Boston defeated the fifth-seeded [Tampa Bay Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Lightning "Tampa Bay Lightning") in seven games in the Eastern Conference Final.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-50) The series began on June 1 with a 1–0 Canucks victory. Roberto Luongo picked up his third shutout of the playoffs while forward [Raffi Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffi_Torres "Raffi Torres") scored the dramatic lone goal with 18.5 seconds remaining in the third period.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-51) However, after Game 1, the series became heated and physical, after Alexandre Burrows apparently bit the finger of Bruins' forward [Patrice Bergeron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrice_Bergeron "Patrice Bergeron") during game one (after the incident was reviewed by the league Burrows was not suspended) and in Game 3, a hit by defenceman [Aaron Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rome "Aaron Rome") left Bruins winger [Nathan Horton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Horton "Nathan Horton") concussed and unable to play for the rest of the series.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-52) Despite playing without Horton – one of the Bruins best goal scorers – for the final four games of the series, Boston was able to pick up their play and comeback to win the series in seven despite staking Vancouver leads of 2–0 and 3–2. It was Boston's first Stanley Cup victory in 39 years. The Canucks became the first team to lose in the Finals after winning the Presidents' Trophy since the [Detroit Red Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_Detroit_Red_Wings_season "1994–95 Detroit Red Wings season") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Stanley_Cup_Final "1995 Stanley Cup Final"). The Canucks 54 wins was the most by a team that lost in the Stanley Cup Finals, surpassing the previous record of 53 by the [Philadelphia Flyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Philadelphia_Flyers_season "1984–85 Philadelphia Flyers season") in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Stanley_Cup_Final "1985 Stanley Cup Final") and 117 points was the most by a team that lost in the final, surpassing the previous record of 116 by the Flyers in [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Stanley_Cup_Final "1980 Stanley Cup Final").

### Broadcast changes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Broadcast changes")]

#### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Television")]

On July 28, 2010, the Vancouver Canucks announced a new partnership with [Rogers Sportsnet One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Sportsnet_One "Rogers Sportsnet One"), a new national sports channel with regional broadcast capabilities. The new partnership included 13 additional games, on top of the 45 on [Rogers Sportsnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Sportsnet "Rogers Sportsnet") Pacific, to be shown thus eliminating Canucks TV Pay-Per-View. In addition, [CBC Hockey Night in Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockey_Night_in_Canada "Hockey Night in Canada") announced that it would once again be showing 14 games nationally while [TSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL_on_TSN "NHL on TSN") would show 10 games.

#### Radio

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Radio")]

Also on July 28, 2010, [Tom Larscheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Larscheid "Tom Larscheid") announced that he would be retiring at the start of the season. His final radio call was during the Vancouver Canucks season opener against the Los Angeles Kings on October 9. He spent 33 years as the colour commentator for the Vancouver Canucks and was replaced by [Dave Tomlinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Tomlinson "Dave Tomlinson").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-53)

The **[2010–11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_NHL_season "2010–11 NHL season")[Vancouver Canucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Canucks "Vancouver Canucks") season** was the 41st season in the modern Canucks history. The [Vancouver Canucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Canucks "Vancouver Canucks") won their fifth [Northwest division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Division_(NHL) "Northwest Division (NHL)") title, third conference championship and first [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-3) They also reached the [Stanley Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup_Final "Stanley Cup Final") for the third time in franchise history, losing to the [Boston Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Bruins "Boston Bruins") in seven games. This marked the last time a Canadian team contended in the Stanley Cup Final until the [Montreal Canadiens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal_Canadiens "Montreal Canadiens") did so in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Stanley_Cup_Final "2021 Stanley Cup Final"), ten years later.

As of the [2025-26 NHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025-26_NHL_season "2025-26 NHL season"), this is the most recent Presidents’ Trophy winner to reach the Finals in a full 82-game season.

## Events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Events")]

### Off-season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Off-season")]

#### Entry draft

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Entry draft")]

The [2010 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NHL_entry_draft "2010 NHL entry draft") was held June 25–26, 2010, at [Staples Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), California. The Canucks had the 25th overall draft choice in the first round as a result of being defeated by the [Chicago Blackhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks") in the [Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_(NHL) "Western Conference (NHL)") semi-final, but that draft choice was traded to the [Florida Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Panthers "Florida Panthers"). The Canucks also did not have a second- or third-round draft pick. Their second-round pick was traded to the [Buffalo Sabres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Sabres "Buffalo Sabres") in exchange for [Steve Bernier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Bernier "Steve Bernier").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-4) Their third-round pick was traded to the [Carolina Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Hurricanes "Carolina Hurricanes") at the NHL trade deadline in exchange for [Andrew Alberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Alberts "Andrew Alberts").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-5) The Canucks acquired an additional sixth-round draft choice from the [Phoenix Coyotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Coyotes "Arizona Coyotes") as a result of a trade that sent [Mathieu Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathieu_Schneider "Mathieu Schneider") to Phoenix.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-mschneider-6) Vancouver had the 115th, 145th, 172nd, 175th and 205th overall draft choices.

#### Trades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Trades")]

On June 25, 2010, the Canucks acquired [Keith Ballard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Ballard "Keith Ballard") and [Victor Oreskovich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Oreskovich "Victor Oreskovich") from the [Florida Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Panthers "Florida Panthers") in exchange for [Steve Bernier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Bernier "Steve Bernier"), [Michael Grabner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Grabner "Michael Grabner") and the 25th overall pick in the 2010 NHL Entry Draft.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-ballard-7)

Mike Gillis traded [Shane O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_O'Brien_(ice_hockey) "Shane O'Brien (ice hockey)") and Dan Gendur to the [Nashville Predators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Predators "Nashville Predators") in exchange for [Ryan Parent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Parent "Ryan Parent") and [Jonas Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Andersson_(ice_hockey) "Jonas Andersson (ice hockey)") on October 5, 2010. Parent was immediately waived after being acquired while Andersson was assigned to the [Manitoba Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba_Moose "Manitoba Moose") (now St. John's Ice Caps) of the [American Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-obtrade-8) On October 6, [Darcy Hordichuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darcy_Hordichuk "Darcy Hordichuk") was traded to the Florida Panthers in exchange for [Andrew Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Peters "Andrew Peters"). Peters would play for the Manitoba Moose.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-apeters-9)

On October 7, Mike Gillis made another trade with the Florida Panthers, this time acquiring [Nathan Paetsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Paetsch "Nathan Paetsch") for [Sean Zimmerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Zimmerman "Sean Zimmerman").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-npaetsch-10)

#### Player signings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Player signings")]

On April 6, 2010, the Canucks signed Swedish [goaltender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goaltender "Goaltender")[Eddie Läck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_L%C3%A4ck "Eddie Läck") to a two-year entry-level contract.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-lack-11) Lack spent the 2009–10 season as a member of the [Brynäs IF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryn%C3%A4s_IF "Brynäs IF"), posting a 2.67 [goals against average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goals_against_average "Goals against average") (GAA) and a .911 [save percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_percentage "Save percentage"). He was expected to start the year with the Manitoba Moose.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-12)

On May 31, 2010, the Canucks announced that they signed three defencemen, including prospect [Yann Sauvé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yann_Sauv%C3%A9 "Yann Sauvé"). Sauvé was drafted 41st overall by the Canucks in the [2008 draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NHL_Entry_Draft "2008 NHL Entry Draft"). In addition, they signed free agent [Lee Sweatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Sweatt "Lee Sweatt") and [Christopher Tanev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Tanev "Christopher Tanev"). Sweatt split time in the Finnish [SM-liiga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liiga "Liiga") and [Kontinental Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kontinental_Hockey_League "Kontinental Hockey League") (KHL) for the 2009–10 season. He registered nine goals and seven assists in 21 games for [TPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TPS_(ice_hockey) "TPS (ice hockey)") in Finland. Sweatt added two goals and five assists in 37 games in the KHL with [Dinamo Riga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinamo_Riga "Dinamo Riga"). Christopher Tanev signed as a free agent after playing in the [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Hockey "Atlantic Hockey"), where he scored 10 goals and 18 assists in 41 games for the [RIT Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIT_Tigers_men's_ice_hockey "RIT Tigers men's ice hockey").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-3d-13)

On June 1, 2010, Vancouver signed [Anton Rödin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_R%C3%B6din "Anton Rödin") to a three-year, entry-level contract. Rödin was drafted 53rd overall by the Canucks in the [2009 Draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NHL_Entry_Draft "2009 NHL Entry Draft"). He spent the 2009–10 season in the [Swedish Elite League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Hockey_League "Swedish Hockey League") with Brynäs IF. He also played at the [2010 World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_World_Junior_Ice_Hockey_Championships "2010 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships"), where he won a bronze medal with Sweden. He finished the tournament tied for second in scoring for Sweden with three goals and ten points, good enough for ninth in the tournament.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-14)

On June 2, 2010, Mike Gillis signed [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider") to a contract extension with the team. He was drafted in the first round, 26th overall, of the [2004 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NHL_entry_draft "2004 NHL entry draft") by the Canucks. He spent the last two seasons playing with the [Manitoba Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba_Moose "Manitoba Moose") of the AHL, where he was named the League's [Goaltender of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldege_%22Baz%22_Bastien_Memorial_Award "Aldege \"Baz\" Bastien Memorial Award") in [2008–09](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_AHL_season "2008–09 AHL season") while leading the Moose to the [Calder Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Calder_Cup_Playoffs "2009 Calder Cup Playoffs").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-cschneider-15) The Canucks also announced that they signed [Peter Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Andersson_(ice_hockey_b._1991) "Peter Andersson (ice hockey b. 1991)") to an entry-level contract. Andersson was drafted 143rd overall by the Canucks in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NHL_Entry_Draft "2009 NHL Entry Draft").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-16)

On June 16, 2010, the Vancouver Canucks re-signed pending unrestricted free agent [Aaron Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rome "Aaron Rome") to a two-year contract. The deal is worth $1.5 million and will have a [salary cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL_Salary_Cap "NHL Salary Cap") hit of $750,000 per season.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-arome-17) On July 2, 2010, [Alexandre Bolduc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Bolduc "Alexandre Bolduc") signed a one-year, two-way contract worth $500,000.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-bolduc-18)[Shane O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_O'Brien_(ice_hockey) "Shane O'Brien (ice hockey)") re-signed with the Canucks on July 6, 2010, when he accepted his qualifying offer. The new contract will pay O'Brien $1.6 million for one year.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-sob-19)[Tanner Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanner_Glass "Tanner Glass") also signed a one-year contract worth $625,000.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-tglass-20)

On July 22, [Jannik Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jannik_Hansen "Jannik Hansen") was awarded a one-year contract worth $825,000 by an arbitrator.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-jhansen-21)

On July 26, the Canucks re-signed [Mason Raymond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Raymond "Mason Raymond") to a new two-year contract worth a total of $5.1 million.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-mraymond-22)

#### Free agency

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Free agency")]

On July 1, the Vancouver Canucks signed [Dan Hamhuis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Hamhuis "Dan Hamhuis") to a six-year contract worth $27 million,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-hamhuis-23)[Jeff Tambellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Tambellini "Jeff Tambellini") to a 1-year contract worth $500,000,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-jtambellini-24)[Manny Malhotra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manny_Malhotra "Manny Malhotra") to a three-year contract worth $7.5 million and [Joel Perrault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Perrault "Joel Perrault") to a one-year contract worth $510,000.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-july1-25) The Canucks signed [Tyler Weiman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Weiman "Tyler Weiman") on July 12 to a one-year contract worth $500,000.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-tweiman-26)

On August 19, Vancouver signed unrestricted free agent [Bill Sweatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Sweatt "Bill Sweatt"), the younger brother of Lee Sweatt, to a three-year, entry-level contract worth $2.7 million. The contract also includes an additional $300,000 per season in potential performance bonuses. Bill Sweatt was drafted 38th overall by the [Chicago Blackhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks") in [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NHL_Entry_Draft "2007 NHL Entry Draft"), but decided not to sign a contract until completing four years of college. He was subsequently traded to the [Toronto Maple Leafs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Maple_Leafs "Toronto Maple Leafs") along with [Kris Versteeg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Versteeg "Kris Versteeg"), but maintained his desire to test free agency. He eventually decided to re-unite with his brother in Vancouver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-bsweatt-27)

The Canucks signed unrestricted free agent [Raffi Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffi_Torres "Raffi Torres") to a one-year contract worth $1 million on August 25.

On October 7, the Canucks signed [Peter Schaefer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Schaefer_(ice_hockey) "Peter Schaefer (ice hockey)") to a one-year, two-way contract worth $600,000. Schaefer played for the Canucks between 1998 and 2000 before being traded to the [Ottawa Senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa_Senators "Ottawa Senators") for [Sami Salo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Salo "Sami Salo").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-pschaefer-28)

### Pre-season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Pre-season")]

#### Training camp

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Training camp")]

The Canucks held their training camp in [Penticton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penticton "Penticton"), British Columbia, at the [South Okanagan Events Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Okanagan_Events_Centre "South Okanagan Events Centre"). In addition to training camp, the Canucks hosted a Young Stars prospect tournament prior to the start of training camp from September 12 to 16. The event featured prospects from five teams in an eight-game round robin format. The tournament included the [Anaheim Ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim_Ducks "Anaheim Ducks"), [Calgary Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Flames "Calgary Flames"), [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton_Oilers "Edmonton Oilers") and [San Jose Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose_Sharks "San Jose Sharks"). The Canucks finished the tournament with a record of 2–2.

Shortly before the start of training camp, [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo") announced that he would be relinquishing his captaincy. Luongo served as the team captain for two seasons.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-luongocpt-29) Forward [Henrik Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin"), was named team captain.

#### Schedule

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Schedule")]

The Canucks' pre-season schedule began on September 21 against the Calgary Flames. It will be a split series where each franchise will split into two squads to play two simultaneous games, one at the [Saddledome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pengrowth_Saddledome "Pengrowth Saddledome") in Calgary and one at [Rogers Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Arena "Rogers Arena") in Vancouver.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-split-30) In addition, the Canucks will play each of the Edmonton Oilers, Anaheim Ducks and San Jose Sharks twice, once at home and once on the road.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-31) The Canucks finished the preseason with a record of 3–5.

### Regular season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Regular season")]

#### Schedule

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Schedule")]

The Canucks officially kicked off their 2010–11 campaign on October 9 at Rogers Arena against the [Los Angeles Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Kings "Los Angeles Kings"). With the Canucks celebrating their 40th anniversary, the NHL scheduled this game to honour the Canucks' first-ever NHL game against the Los Angeles Kings on October 9, 1970. The Canucks lost the game in a shootout by a score of 2–1. They began the season slowly, going 2–3–1 in their first six games before going on a six-game winning streak. The loss to break the streak came as part of a five-game road trip where they recorded a 2–2–1 record before returning home for their most lopsided loss of the year, a 7–1 defeat at the hands of the [Chicago Blackhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks"). Following the loss the Canucks went 18–4–3, which included an eight-game winning streak, and two four-game winning streaks, before losing three consecutive games in extra time. They proceeded to win the next six games, but ended February alternating wins and losses. Vancouver's win against the [Minnesota Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Wild "Minnesota Wild") on March 14, 2011, put the team at 101 points in the standings. It was the fastest the Canucks reached the 100-point mark in franchise history.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-33) Next, the team recorded its 50th victory of the season for the first time in franchise history on March 27.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-34) They would get top seed in the Western Conference on 2 days later.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-35) And it would get its first [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") two days later.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-36) The season finale took place on April 9, 2011, against the Calgary Flames, which saw the Canucks win 3–2 in overtime. Daniel Sedin registered two assists in order to clinch the [Art Ross Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Ross_Trophy "Art Ross Trophy"), a year after his brother did it.

Excluding four shootout-winning goals, the Canucks scored 258 goals, the most in the League. Furthermore, excluding their five shootout goals allowed, the Canucks gave up only 180 goals in their 82 games, the fewest in the League. They also scored the most power-play goals, with 72, and had the best power-play percentage, at 24.32% (72 for 296).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-38)

The Canucks were also the first team since the [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Stanley_Cup_Final "1978 Stanley Cup Final") champion [Montreal Canadiens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977%E2%80%9378_Montreal_Canadiens_season "1977–78 Montreal Canadiens season") to finish the league with the most goals scored and fewest goals against. They also finished the regular season with the top ranked power play and third ranked penalty kill. They almost finished the same identical record as the [1988–89 Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988%E2%80%9389_Calgary_Flames_season "1988–89 Calgary Flames season") (except they had two fewer losses).

#### Special events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Special events")]

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Orland_Kurtenbach_ring_of_honour.jpg/330px-Orland_Kurtenbach_ring_of_honour.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Orland_Kurtenbach_ring_of_honour.jpg)

[Orland Kurtenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orland_Kurtenbach "Orland Kurtenbach")'s plaque on the Canucks' Ring of Honour in Rogers Arena.

The Canucks kicked off their season with a [pre-game ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-game_ceremony "Pre-game ceremony") on October 9, 2010, to commemorate their 40th Anniversary. They also announced Henrik Sedin as the 13th captain of the team.

Prior to their game on December 11, 2010, against the [Tampa Bay Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Lightning "Tampa Bay Lightning"), the Canucks honoured [Markus Näslund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_N%C3%A4slund "Markus Näslund") by retiring his number 19 jersey. Näslund was the third player in franchise history to receive the honour following [Stan Smyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Smyl "Stan Smyl") and [Trevor Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Linden "Trevor Linden"). Näslund spent 12 seasons with the Canucks, nine as captain. He also holds the franchise lead in points scored with 756. The retirement ceremony coincided with [Mattias Öhlund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattias_%C3%96hlund "Mattias Öhlund")'s return to Vancouver for the first time since signing with the Lightning in 2009.

The Canucks also announced that they will be introducing a "Ring of Honour" to commemorate past players. Four players will have their names added to the ring this season. The first player to get the honour will be [Orland Kurtenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orland_Kurtenbach "Orland Kurtenbach") who was the first ever captain of the Vancouver Canucks. Kurtenbach's ceremony took place on October 26. [Kirk McLean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirk_McLean "Kirk McLean") was added to the ring of honour on November 24. McLean helped lead the Canucks to game seven of the [1994 Stanley Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Stanley_Cup_Final "1994 Stanley Cup Final"). The third player to be inducted into the Ring of Honour will be [Thomas Gradin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Gradin "Thomas Gradin") on January 24. Gradin was part of the 1982 Canucks team that made it to the Stanley Cup Final. He now works as a European scout for organization and is heavily praised at having convinced then-general manager [Dave Nonis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Nonis "Dave Nonis") to draft [Alexander Edler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Edler "Alexander Edler").

The final ceremony took place on March 14 when [Harold Snepsts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Snepsts "Harold Snepsts") was inducted into the Ring of Honour.

### Playoffs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Playoffs")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Henrik_Sedin_accepts_the_trophy.jpg/250px-Henrik_Sedin_accepts_the_trophy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Henrik_Sedin_accepts_the_trophy.jpg)

[Henrik Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin") accepts the [Clarence S. Campbell Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_S._Campbell_Bowl "Clarence S. Campbell Bowl") after the Vancouver Canucks beat the San Jose Sharks to win the Western Conference finals

The Vancouver Canucks were the first team in the NHL to clinch a berth in the playoffs. Two weeks later, they clinched their division on March 16.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-39) The win earned them their fourth [Northwest Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Division_(NHL) "Northwest Division (NHL)") title in five years, thus guaranteeing them home ice advantage in the first round of the [Stanley Cup playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Stanley_Cup_playoffs "2011 Stanley Cup playoffs"). This was the fastest the team had clinched a playoff spot in franchise history.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-playoffsclinch-40) The team earned the top seed in the Western Conference on March 29 and the [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") two days later, guaranteeing home ice advantage throughout the playoffs.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-41)

The Canucks opened their post-season schedule with a series against the eighth-seeded and defending [Stanley Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup "Stanley Cup") champion [Chicago Blackhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-42) This was the third time the two teams played in the playoffs in consecutive years with the Blackhawks winning the first two, both in the second round in six games.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-43) Vancouver won the opening three games of the series before Chicago responded by winning the next three games to force a game seven. [Alexandre Burrows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Burrows "Alexandre Burrows") scored the winning goal in game 7 in overtime on Blackhawks' goaltender [Corey Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Crawford "Corey Crawford") to clinch the 2–1 victory in the game and 4–3 series victory.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-44)

Vancouver moved on to play the fifth-seeded [Nashville Predators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Predators "Nashville Predators") in the second round of the playoffs. It is the first time the two teams had met in the playoffs.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-45) Vancouver won the first game before Nashville won game two to even up the series at one.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-46) Vancouver won both games in Nashville, Game 3 3–2 in overtime on a [Ryan Kesler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Kesler "Ryan Kesler") deflection goal and 4–2 in Game 4, respectively.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-47) The series returned to Vancouver for Game 5 with the Canucks having a 3–1 series lead, where the Predators staved off elimination by beating the Canucks 4–3 and Predators' forward [Joel Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Ward_(ice_hockey) "Joel Ward (ice hockey)") scored two goals, including the game winner to force a game six. The Canucks won the series 4–2 after a 2–1 victory in Game 6 in Nashville to clinch their first Western Conference Final appearance since 1994.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-48)

The Canucks played the second-seeded [San Jose Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose_Sharks "San Jose Sharks") for the first time ever in the [Western Conference Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_(NHL) "Western Conference (NHL)") after San Jose eliminated the third-seeded [Detroit Red Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Red_Wings "Detroit Red Wings") in Game 7. Vancouver prevailed in five games with a double overtime goal scored by defenceman [Kevin Bieksa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Bieksa "Kevin Bieksa") in Game 5 in Vancouver to send the Canucks to the [Stanley Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup_Final "Stanley Cup Final") for the third time in franchise history and the first time since 1994.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-49)

They would face the third-seeded [Boston Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Bruins "Boston Bruins") after Boston defeated the fifth-seeded [Tampa Bay Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Lightning "Tampa Bay Lightning") in seven games in the Eastern Conference Final.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-50) The series began on June 1 with a 1–0 Canucks victory. Roberto Luongo picked up his third shutout of the playoffs while forward [Raffi Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffi_Torres "Raffi Torres") scored the dramatic lone goal with 18.5 seconds remaining in the third period.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-51) However, after Game 1, the series became heated and physical, after Alexandre Burrows apparently bit the finger of Bruins' forward [Patrice Bergeron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrice_Bergeron "Patrice Bergeron") during game one (after the incident was reviewed by the league Burrows was not suspended) and in Game 3, a hit by defenceman [Aaron Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rome "Aaron Rome") left Bruins winger [Nathan Horton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Horton "Nathan Horton") concussed and unable to play for the rest of the series.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-52) Despite playing without Horton – one of the Bruins best goal scorers – for the final four games of the series, Boston was able to pick up their play and comeback to win the series in seven despite staking Vancouver leads of 2–0 and 3–2. It was Boston's first Stanley Cup victory in 39 years. The Canucks became the first team to lose in the Finals after winning the Presidents' Trophy since the [Detroit Red Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_Detroit_Red_Wings_season "1994–95 Detroit Red Wings season") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_Stanley_Cup_Final "1995 Stanley Cup Final"). The Canucks 54 wins was the most by a team that lost in the Stanley Cup Finals, surpassing the previous record of 53 by the [Philadelphia Flyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Philadelphia_Flyers_season "1984–85 Philadelphia Flyers season") in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Stanley_Cup_Final "1985 Stanley Cup Final") and 117 points was the most by a team that lost in the final, surpassing the previous record of 116 by the Flyers in [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Stanley_Cup_Final "1980 Stanley Cup Final").

#### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010%E2%80%9311_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Television")]

On July 28, 2010, the Vancouver Canucks announced a new partnership with [Rogers Sportsnet One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Sportsnet_One "Rogers Sportsnet One"), a new national sports channel with regional broadcast capabilities. The new partnership included 13 additional games, on top of the 45 on [Rogers Sportsnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Sportsnet "Rogers Sportsnet") Pacific, to be shown thus eliminating Canucks TV Pay-Per-View. In addition, [CBC Hockey Night in Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockey_Night_in_Canada "Hockey Night in Canada") announced that it would once again be showing 14 games nationally while [TSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL_on_TSN "NHL on TSN") would show 10 games.
