Canucks season")→ | The **2011–12 Vancouver Canucks season** was the 42nd season in the modern Canucks history. The [Vancouver Canucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Canucks "Vancouver Canucks") were the defending [Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_(NHL) "Western Conference (NHL)") champions and three time defending [Northwest Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Division_(NHL) "Northwest Division (NHL)") champions. The Canucks opened the regular season against the [Pittsburgh Penguins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Penguins "Pittsburgh Penguins") at home on October 6, 2011. Their final regular season game was held at [Rogers Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Arena "Rogers Arena") against the [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton_Oilers "Edmonton Oilers") on April 7, 2012. The Canucks entered the season expected to again contend for their first ever [Stanley Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup "Stanley Cup") after coming one win short from winning it the previous season and maintaining the majority of the players from the previous season on the roster. The Canucks struggled out of the gate, hovering around .500 until roughly the 20-game mark due to weak defensive play and a slow start from starting goaltender [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo"). The Canucks then recovered by the 20th game on November 20 against the [Ottawa Senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa_Senators "Ottawa Senators") (where they defeated the Senators 2–1) and would go on to play their best hockey of the season from that day until the end of February. The team dominated much like they did the season prior during this stretch from late-November to late-February, as goals came in bunches and the offense was backed up by strong goaltending from the tandem of Luongo and backup goaltender [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider"). The peak of the Canucks' season came on January 7, 2012, in the 42nd game of the season which came against the [Boston Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Bruins "Boston Bruins"), a rematch of the [2011 Stanley Cup Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Stanley_Cup_Finals "2011 Stanley Cup Finals"). The Canucks prevailed 4–3 in a fight-filled game with a hard-fought playoff atmosphere, and they seemed to state to the hockey world that they would be heard from again come playoff time if they were to meet in the Stanley Cup Finals again. Despite their continuation of winning lengthy stretches of games within the last several weeks from early-March to early-April, the team did not play with the same heart they played with earlier in the season as they often played down to their competition by barely beating some of the weakest teams in the league and even lost games they had little business losing as the offense seemed to disappear and the team was lucky to have maintained outstanding goaltending and defense that kept them in games and eventually leading them to their second consecutive [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") and second Presidents' Trophy in franchise history altogether on the final day of the season on April 7, when they defeated the Edmonton Oilers 3–0 and the top seeded Eastern Conference team [New York Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Rangers "New York Rangers") lost their season finale the same day 4–1 against the [Washington Capitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Capitals "Washington Capitals"), ending their [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_New_York_Rangers_season "2011–12 New York Rangers season") with 109 points in the standings, two points behind the Canucks 111 points. Despite entering the [2012 playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Stanley_Cup_playoffs "2012 Stanley Cup playoffs") as the top seed in the Western Conference for the second year in a row and the back-to-back Presidents' Trophy winners, the Canucks were upset in the first round in five games by the eight-seeded [Los Angeles Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Kings "Los Angeles Kings"), who would eventually go on to win their first Stanley Cup in franchise history as the weeks went on, making them the first, and so far only team to do so. This marked the third consecutive season and fourth time in six seasons where the Canucks lost a playoff series to an eventual Stanley Cup champion. ## Off-season [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Off-season")] ### NHL entry draft [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: NHL entry draft")] [![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Nicklas_Jensen_2011_NHL_Draft.jpg/250px-Nicklas_Jensen_2011_NHL_Draft.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nicklas_Jensen_2011_NHL_Draft.jpg) Nicklas Jensen on stage after being selected 29th overall in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft Main article: [2011 NHL Entry Draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NHL_Entry_Draft "2011 NHL Entry Draft") The [2011 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NHL_entry_draft "2011 NHL entry draft") was held June 24–25, 2011, at the [Xcel Energy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcel_Energy_Center "Xcel Energy Center") in [Saint Paul, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Paul,_Minnesota "Saint Paul, Minnesota"). The Canucks selected eight players including [Nicklas Jensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicklas_Jensen "Nicklas Jensen") with their first-round draft choice, 29th overall. On day two of the entry draft the Vancouver Canucks traded their second-round draft choice to the [Minnesota Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Wild "Minnesota Wild") for two picks in later rounds. In total, Vancouver selected eight players including [David Honzík](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Honz%C3%ADk "David Honzík"), [Alexandre Grenier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Grenier "Alexandre Grenier"), [Joseph LaBate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_LaBate "Joseph LaBate"), [Ludwig Blomstrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Blomstrand "Ludwig Blomstrand"), [Frank Corrado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Corrado "Frank Corrado"), Pathrik Westerholm and [Henrik Tommernes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_T%C3%B6mmernes "Henrik Tömmernes"). In total, none would become regular NHL players, with Corrado playing the most games with 76 appearances across three teams. ### Minor League affiliations [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Minor League affiliations")] On June 21, 2011, True North Sports & Entertainment, the owners of the [Manitoba Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba_Moose "Manitoba Moose") received Board of Governors approval to purchase and re-locate the [Atlanta Thrashers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Thrashers "Atlanta Thrashers"). The Thrashers moved to [Winnipeg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg "Winnipeg"), Manitoba to replace the Manitoba Moose. The Moose announced that they were moving to St. John's and would become the [AHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League") affiliate of the [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets "Winnipeg Jets"). As a result, the Canucks were left without an affiliate temporarily. On June 27, 2011, the Vancouver Canucks signed a two-year affiliation agreement with the [Chicago Wolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Wolves "Chicago Wolves").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-wolvesaffiliate-2) The Vancouver Canucks announced that [Craig MacTavish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_MacTavish "Craig MacTavish") would be the new coach for the Wolves on August 1 after [Claude Noel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_No%C3%ABl "Claude Noël"), who coached the Manitoba Moose during the 2010–11 season, was hired by the Jets.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-3) In addition, on April 8, 2011, it was announced that the [Chilliwack Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilliwack_Bruins "Chilliwack Bruins") of the [Western Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hockey_League "Western Hockey League") would be moving their franchise to [Victoria, British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_British_Columbia "Victoria, British Columbia").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-4) The sale of the Chilliwack Bruins to RG Properties was completed and made official on April 20 by the WHL.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-bruinssold-5) The [Victoria Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Royals "Victoria Royals") replaced the [Victoria Salmon Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Salmon_Kings "Victoria Salmon Kings") and began play in the [2011–12 WHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_WHL_season "2011–12 WHL season"). RG Properties, who also owned the Victoria Salmon Kings, opted to fold the Salmon Kings franchise at the conclusion of the [2010–11 ECHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_ECHL_season "2010–11 ECHL season").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-salmonkingsfold-6) As a result, the Canucks were left without an [ECHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECHL "ECHL") minor league affiliate. The Salmon Kings spent five years as the ECHL affiliate of the Vancouver Canucks. On September 22, the Vancouver Canucks announced that it had signed an ECHL affiliation agreement with the [Kalamazoo Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalamazoo_Wings "Kalamazoo Wings").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-7) ## Preseason [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Preseason")] Training camp began for the rookies on September 9 and included two days of on-ice training sessions followed by a four-game Young Stars tournament featuring prospects from other teams including the [Calgary Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Flames "Calgary Flames"), [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton_Oilers "Edmonton Oilers"), [San Jose Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose_Sharks "San Jose Sharks") and [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets "Winnipeg Jets"). Among the players were four that were selected from the 2011 Entry Draft. Nicklas Jensen, David Honzik, Alexandre Grenier and Frank Corrado all took part in the Canucks rookie training camp and Young Stars tournament. LaBate did not participate in the camp because his college semester had begun while Blomstrand, Westerholm and Tommernes were in the midst of training camp for their own Swedish hockey clubs. The Vancouver Canucks main training camp started on September 16. Several veteran NHL players were invited to the camp on a try-out basis. These players included [Owen Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Nolan "Owen Nolan"), [Anders Eriksson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anders_Eriksson_(ice_hockey_b._1975) "Anders Eriksson (ice hockey b. 1975)"), [Niko Dimitrakos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niko_Dimitrakos "Niko Dimitrakos") and [Todd Fedoruk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Fedoruk "Todd Fedoruk"). However, none of the invites were able to secure a contract with the club. The Canucks played a total of eight preseason games where they finished with a record of 3–5. Much of the Vancouver Canucks roster were returning members from the 2010–11 season with the exception of [Christian Ehrhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Ehrhoff "Christian Ehrhoff") and [Raffi Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffi_Torres "Raffi Torres"), who both changed teams, through trade and free agency respectively, during the off-season. Citing the shortened off-season due to their appearance in the [Stanley Cup Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Stanley_Cup_Finals "2011 Stanley Cup Finals"), the Vancouver Canucks management and coaching staff decided to give a majority of the veterans rest. As a result, players guaranteed roster spots in the regular season, such as [Daniel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Sedin "Daniel Sedin") and [Henrik Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin") only played in two preseason games. ## Regular season [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Regular season")] Like 2010–11, the Canucks were met with extremely high expectations for the upcoming season. They entered 2011–12 as the defending [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") and [Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_(NHL) "Western Conference (NHL)") champions. It was a record setting season that saw them rank first in the league in goals per game, goals against per game and power play percentage. Both [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo") and [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider") were awarded the [William M. Jennings Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_M._Jennings_Trophy "William M. Jennings Trophy") for lowest goals against. General consensus through various sports media outlets such as [The Hockey News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hockey_News "The Hockey News"), [Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated"), [TSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sports_Network "The Sports Network") and [Sportsnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportsnet "Sportsnet") predicted that the Canucks would return to the Western Conference Finals or at least finish first in the Western Conference regular season.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-9) ### October–November [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: October–November")] [![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/37_RYP_Patch.svg/250px-37_RYP_Patch.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:37_RYP_Patch.svg) Helmet decal worn by the Vancouver Canucks team throughout the season The Vancouver Canucks began their season on October 6 when they hosted the [Pittsburgh Penguins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Penguins "Pittsburgh Penguins") before embarking on a four-game road trip. Prior to the start of the home opener the Canucks organization held a ceremony to celebrate their 2010–11 season and to thank the police officers, [firemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firefighter "Firefighter") and volunteers who helped the city recover after the [Stanley Cup riot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Vancouver_Stanley_Cup_riot "2011 Vancouver Stanley Cup riot"). The game was supposed to be [Sidney Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Crosby "Sidney Crosby")'s third NHL game at [Rogers Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Arena "Rogers Arena"), and first hockey game since scoring the [golden goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_goal#Ice_hockey "Golden goal") at the [2010 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey_at_the_2010_Winter_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament") but was unable to play as he was still recovering from a [concussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concussion "Concussion"). In the game, the Vancouver Canucks battled back from a 3–1 deficit but fell short in a shootout. The club held a ceremony on October 18 prior to their game against the [New York Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Rangers "New York Rangers") to honour the late [Rick Rypien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Rypien "Rick Rypien"). Rypien played within the Vancouver Canucks organization for seven seasons, splitting time between the Canucks and the [Manitoba Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba_Moose "Manitoba Moose"), before signing with the [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets "Winnipeg Jets") during the summer. Rypien was found dead at his home in [Crowsnest Pass, Alberta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowsnest_Pass,_Alberta "Crowsnest Pass, Alberta"), on August 15. The Canucks wore a helmet decal in honour of Rypien during the season.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-rypienceremony-10) The Canucks also ran a video tribute for former Ranger [Derek Boogaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Boogaard "Derek Boogaard") who also died during the off-season.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-11) The Canucks struggled throughout the month of October which was punctuated by a significant trade. Mikael Samuelsson and [Marco Sturm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Sturm "Marco Sturm") were traded to the Florida Panthers on October 22, just hours after the Canucks defeated the [Minnesota Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Wild "Minnesota Wild"). In return, the Canucks acquired a third-round draft pick in the [2013 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NHL_entry_draft "2013 NHL entry draft") and [forwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_(ice_hockey) "Forward (ice hockey)")[David Booth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Booth_(ice_hockey) "David Booth (ice hockey)") and [Steven Reinprecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Reinprecht "Steven Reinprecht"). The month ended with a match up against the [Washington Capitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Capitals "Washington Capitals") that saw the Canucks prevail by a final score of 7–4. [Alex Edler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Edler "Alexander Edler"), Maxim Lapierre and [Chris Higgins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Higgins_(ice_hockey) "Chris Higgins (ice hockey)") all registered two goals for Vancouver while [Alexander Ovechkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Ovechkin "Alexander Ovechkin") also scored a pair of goals for Washington. The month of November opened with a six-game road trip beginning in [Calgary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Flames "Calgary Flames"), where the Canucks won the game by a score of 5–1. The game saw Daniel Sedin score his 254th goal of his career to tie [Pavel Bure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Bure "Pavel Bure") for fourth all-time in Canucks goal scoring. However, the Canucks continued to battle inconsistency and were unable to sustain any momentum through the first two-thirds of the month where they compiled a record of 4–4 capped by a blowout loss to rival [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks"). The Canucks, led by [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider") who originally replaced an injured [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo"), finished the month with five consecutive victories that included back-to-back shutouts for Schneider. During the winning streak head coach [Alain Vigneault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Vigneault "Alain Vigneault") became the team's winningest coach when the team defeated [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Avalanche "Colorado Avalanche") on November 23.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-12) ## The **2011–12 Vancouver Canucks season** was the 42nd season in the modern Canucks history. The [Vancouver Canucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Canucks "Vancouver Canucks") were the defending [Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_(NHL) "Western Conference (NHL)") champions and three time defending [Northwest Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Division_(NHL) "Northwest Division (NHL)") champions. The Canucks opened the regular season against the [Pittsburgh Penguins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Penguins "Pittsburgh Penguins") at home on October 6, 2011. Their final regular season game was held at [Rogers Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Arena "Rogers Arena") against the [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton_Oilers "Edmonton Oilers") on April 7, 2012.

The Canucks entered the season expected to again contend for their first ever [Stanley Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup "Stanley Cup") after coming one win short from winning it the previous season and maintaining the majority of the players from the previous season on the roster. The Canucks struggled out of the gate, hovering around .500 until roughly the 20-game mark due to weak defensive play and a slow start from starting goaltender [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo"). The Canucks then recovered by the 20th game on November 20 against the [Ottawa Senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottawa_Senators "Ottawa Senators") (where they defeated the Senators 2–1) and would go on to play their best hockey of the season from that day until the end of February. The team dominated much like they did the season prior during this stretch from late-November to late-February, as goals came in bunches and the offense was backed up by strong goaltending from the tandem of Luongo and backup goaltender [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider"). The peak of the Canucks' season came on January 7, 2012, in the 42nd game of the season which came against the [Boston Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Bruins "Boston Bruins"), a rematch of the [2011 Stanley Cup Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Stanley_Cup_Finals "2011 Stanley Cup Finals"). The Canucks prevailed 4–3 in a fight-filled game with a hard-fought playoff atmosphere, and they seemed to state to the hockey world that they would be heard from again come playoff time if they were to meet in the Stanley Cup Finals again. Despite their continuation of winning lengthy stretches of games within the last several weeks from early-March to early-April, the team did not play with the same heart they played with earlier in the season as they often played down to their competition by barely beating some of the weakest teams in the league and even lost games they had little business losing as the offense seemed to disappear and the team was lucky to have maintained outstanding goaltending and defense that kept them in games and eventually leading them to their second consecutive [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") and second Presidents' Trophy in franchise history altogether on the final day of the season on April 7, when they defeated the Edmonton Oilers 3–0 and the top seeded Eastern Conference team [New York Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Rangers "New York Rangers") lost their season finale the same day 4–1 against the [Washington Capitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Capitals "Washington Capitals"), ending their [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_New_York_Rangers_season "2011–12 New York Rangers season") with 109 points in the standings, two points behind the Canucks 111 points. Despite entering the [2012 playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Stanley_Cup_playoffs "2012 Stanley Cup playoffs") as the top seed in the Western Conference for the second year in a row and the back-to-back Presidents' Trophy winners, the Canucks were upset in the first round in five games by the eight-seeded [Los Angeles Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Kings "Los Angeles Kings"), who would eventually go on to win their first Stanley Cup in franchise history as the weeks went on, making them the first, and so far only team to do so. This marked the third consecutive season and fourth time in six seasons where the Canucks lost a playoff series to an eventual Stanley Cup champion.

## Off-season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Off-season")]

### NHL entry draft

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: NHL entry draft")]

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Nicklas_Jensen_2011_NHL_Draft.jpg/250px-Nicklas_Jensen_2011_NHL_Draft.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nicklas_Jensen_2011_NHL_Draft.jpg)

Nicklas Jensen on stage after being selected 29th overall in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft

Main article: [2011 NHL Entry Draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NHL_Entry_Draft "2011 NHL Entry Draft")

The [2011 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NHL_entry_draft "2011 NHL entry draft") was held June 24–25, 2011, at the [Xcel Energy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcel_Energy_Center "Xcel Energy Center") in [Saint Paul, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Paul,_Minnesota "Saint Paul, Minnesota"). The Canucks selected eight players including [Nicklas Jensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicklas_Jensen "Nicklas Jensen") with their first-round draft choice, 29th overall. On day two of the entry draft the Vancouver Canucks traded their second-round draft choice to the [Minnesota Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Wild "Minnesota Wild") for two picks in later rounds. In total, Vancouver selected eight players including [David Honzík](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Honz%C3%ADk "David Honzík"), [Alexandre Grenier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Grenier "Alexandre Grenier"), [Joseph LaBate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_LaBate "Joseph LaBate"), [Ludwig Blomstrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Blomstrand "Ludwig Blomstrand"), [Frank Corrado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Corrado "Frank Corrado"), Pathrik Westerholm and [Henrik Tommernes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_T%C3%B6mmernes "Henrik Tömmernes"). In total, none would become regular NHL players, with Corrado playing the most games with 76 appearances across three teams.

### Minor League affiliations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Minor League affiliations")]

On June 21, 2011, True North Sports & Entertainment, the owners of the [Manitoba Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba_Moose "Manitoba Moose") received Board of Governors approval to purchase and re-locate the [Atlanta Thrashers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Thrashers "Atlanta Thrashers"). The Thrashers moved to [Winnipeg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg "Winnipeg"), Manitoba to replace the Manitoba Moose. The Moose announced that they were moving to St. John's and would become the [AHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League") affiliate of the [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets "Winnipeg Jets"). As a result, the Canucks were left without an affiliate temporarily. On June 27, 2011, the Vancouver Canucks signed a two-year affiliation agreement with the [Chicago Wolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Wolves "Chicago Wolves").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-wolvesaffiliate-2) The Vancouver Canucks announced that [Craig MacTavish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_MacTavish "Craig MacTavish") would be the new coach for the Wolves on August 1 after [Claude Noel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_No%C3%ABl "Claude Noël"), who coached the Manitoba Moose during the 2010–11 season, was hired by the Jets.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-3)

In addition, on April 8, 2011, it was announced that the [Chilliwack Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilliwack_Bruins "Chilliwack Bruins") of the [Western Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hockey_League "Western Hockey League") would be moving their franchise to [Victoria, British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_British_Columbia "Victoria, British Columbia").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-4) The sale of the Chilliwack Bruins to RG Properties was completed and made official on April 20 by the WHL.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-bruinssold-5) The [Victoria Royals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Royals "Victoria Royals") replaced the [Victoria Salmon Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Salmon_Kings "Victoria Salmon Kings") and began play in the [2011–12 WHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_WHL_season "2011–12 WHL season"). RG Properties, who also owned the Victoria Salmon Kings, opted to fold the Salmon Kings franchise at the conclusion of the [2010–11 ECHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_ECHL_season "2010–11 ECHL season").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-salmonkingsfold-6) As a result, the Canucks were left without an [ECHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECHL "ECHL") minor league affiliate. The Salmon Kings spent five years as the ECHL affiliate of the Vancouver Canucks.

On September 22, the Vancouver Canucks announced that it had signed an ECHL affiliation agreement with the [Kalamazoo Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalamazoo_Wings "Kalamazoo Wings").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-7)

## Preseason

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Preseason")]

Training camp began for the rookies on September 9 and included two days of on-ice training sessions followed by a four-game Young Stars tournament featuring prospects from other teams including the [Calgary Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Flames "Calgary Flames"), [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton_Oilers "Edmonton Oilers"), [San Jose Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose_Sharks "San Jose Sharks") and [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets "Winnipeg Jets"). Among the players were four that were selected from the 2011 Entry Draft. Nicklas Jensen, David Honzik, Alexandre Grenier and Frank Corrado all took part in the Canucks rookie training camp and Young Stars tournament. LaBate did not participate in the camp because his college semester had begun while Blomstrand, Westerholm and Tommernes were in the midst of training camp for their own Swedish hockey clubs.

The Vancouver Canucks main training camp started on September 16. Several veteran NHL players were invited to the camp on a try-out basis. These players included [Owen Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Nolan "Owen Nolan"), [Anders Eriksson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anders_Eriksson_(ice_hockey_b._1975) "Anders Eriksson (ice hockey b. 1975)"), [Niko Dimitrakos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niko_Dimitrakos "Niko Dimitrakos") and [Todd Fedoruk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Fedoruk "Todd Fedoruk"). However, none of the invites were able to secure a contract with the club.

The Canucks played a total of eight preseason games where they finished with a record of 3–5. Much of the Vancouver Canucks roster were returning members from the 2010–11 season with the exception of [Christian Ehrhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Ehrhoff "Christian Ehrhoff") and [Raffi Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffi_Torres "Raffi Torres"), who both changed teams, through trade and free agency respectively, during the off-season.

Citing the shortened off-season due to their appearance in the [Stanley Cup Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Stanley_Cup_Finals "2011 Stanley Cup Finals"), the Vancouver Canucks management and coaching staff decided to give a majority of the veterans rest. As a result, players guaranteed roster spots in the regular season, such as [Daniel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Sedin "Daniel Sedin") and [Henrik Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin") only played in two preseason games.

## Regular season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Regular season")]

Like 2010–11, the Canucks were met with extremely high expectations for the upcoming season. They entered 2011–12 as the defending [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") and [Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_(NHL) "Western Conference (NHL)") champions. It was a record setting season that saw them rank first in the league in goals per game, goals against per game and power play percentage. Both [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo") and [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider") were awarded the [William M. Jennings Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_M._Jennings_Trophy "William M. Jennings Trophy") for lowest goals against.

General consensus through various sports media outlets such as [The Hockey News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hockey_News "The Hockey News"), [Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated"), [TSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sports_Network "The Sports Network") and [Sportsnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportsnet "Sportsnet") predicted that the Canucks would return to the Western Conference Finals or at least finish first in the Western Conference regular season.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-9)

### October–November

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: October–November")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/37_RYP_Patch.svg/250px-37_RYP_Patch.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:37_RYP_Patch.svg)

Helmet decal worn by the Vancouver Canucks team throughout the season

The Vancouver Canucks began their season on October 6 when they hosted the [Pittsburgh Penguins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Penguins "Pittsburgh Penguins") before embarking on a four-game road trip. Prior to the start of the home opener the Canucks organization held a ceremony to celebrate their 2010–11 season and to thank the police officers, [firemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firefighter "Firefighter") and volunteers who helped the city recover after the [Stanley Cup riot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Vancouver_Stanley_Cup_riot "2011 Vancouver Stanley Cup riot"). The game was supposed to be [Sidney Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Crosby "Sidney Crosby")'s third NHL game at [Rogers Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Arena "Rogers Arena"), and first hockey game since scoring the [golden goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_goal#Ice_hockey "Golden goal") at the [2010 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey_at_the_2010_Winter_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament") but was unable to play as he was still recovering from a [concussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concussion "Concussion"). In the game, the Vancouver Canucks battled back from a 3–1 deficit but fell short in a shootout.

The club held a ceremony on October 18 prior to their game against the [New York Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Rangers "New York Rangers") to honour the late [Rick Rypien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Rypien "Rick Rypien"). Rypien played within the Vancouver Canucks organization for seven seasons, splitting time between the Canucks and the [Manitoba Moose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba_Moose "Manitoba Moose"), before signing with the [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg_Jets "Winnipeg Jets") during the summer. Rypien was found dead at his home in [Crowsnest Pass, Alberta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowsnest_Pass,_Alberta "Crowsnest Pass, Alberta"), on August 15. The Canucks wore a helmet decal in honour of Rypien during the season.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-rypienceremony-10) The Canucks also ran a video tribute for former Ranger [Derek Boogaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Boogaard "Derek Boogaard") who also died during the off-season.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-11)

The Canucks struggled throughout the month of October which was punctuated by a significant trade. Mikael Samuelsson and [Marco Sturm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Sturm "Marco Sturm") were traded to the Florida Panthers on October 22, just hours after the Canucks defeated the [Minnesota Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Wild "Minnesota Wild"). In return, the Canucks acquired a third-round draft pick in the [2013 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NHL_entry_draft "2013 NHL entry draft") and [forwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_(ice_hockey) "Forward (ice hockey)")[David Booth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Booth_(ice_hockey) "David Booth (ice hockey)") and [Steven Reinprecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Reinprecht "Steven Reinprecht"). The month ended with a match up against the [Washington Capitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Capitals "Washington Capitals") that saw the Canucks prevail by a final score of 7–4. [Alex Edler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Edler "Alexander Edler"), Maxim Lapierre and [Chris Higgins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Higgins_(ice_hockey) "Chris Higgins (ice hockey)") all registered two goals for Vancouver while [Alexander Ovechkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Ovechkin "Alexander Ovechkin") also scored a pair of goals for Washington.

The month of November opened with a six-game road trip beginning in [Calgary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Flames "Calgary Flames"), where the Canucks won the game by a score of 5–1. The game saw Daniel Sedin score his 254th goal of his career to tie [Pavel Bure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Bure "Pavel Bure") for fourth all-time in Canucks goal scoring. However, the Canucks continued to battle inconsistency and were unable to sustain any momentum through the first two-thirds of the month where they compiled a record of 4–4 capped by a blowout loss to rival [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Blackhawks "Chicago Blackhawks"). The Canucks, led by [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider") who originally replaced an injured [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo"), finished the month with five consecutive victories that included back-to-back shutouts for Schneider. During the winning streak head coach [Alain Vigneault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Vigneault "Alain Vigneault") became the team's winningest coach when the team defeated [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Avalanche "Colorado Avalanche") on November 23.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-12)

### Playoffs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011%E2%80%9312_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Playoffs")]

See also: [2012 Stanley Cup playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Stanley_Cup_playoffs "2012 Stanley Cup playoffs")

The Vancouver Canucks clinched the [Presidents' Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidents'_Trophy "Presidents' Trophy") for the second consecutive year and second time in franchise history, thus guaranteeing themselves home ice advantage for the duration of the playoffs regardless of how far they were to go. However, they were knocked out in the first round by the eighth-seeded and eventual Stanley Cup champion [Los Angeles Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Kings "Los Angeles Kings").

The [[Vancouver Canucks]] were the defending [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] champions and three time defending [[Northwest Division (NHL)|Northwest Division]] champions. The Canucks opened the regular season against the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] at home on October 6, 2011. Their final regular season game was held at [[Rogers Arena]] against the [[Edmonton Oilers]] on April 7, 2012. The Canucks entered the season expected to again contend for their first ever [[Stanley Cup]] after coming one win short from winning it the [[2010–11 Vancouver Canucks season|previous season]] and maintaining the majority of the players from the previous season on the roster. The Canucks struggled out of the gate, hovering around .500 until roughly the 20-game mark due to weak defensive play and a slow start from starting goaltender [[Roberto Luongo]]. The Canucks then recovered by the 20th game on November 20 against the [[Ottawa Senators]] (where they defeated the Senators 2–1) and would go on to play their best hockey of the season from that day until the end of February. The team dominated much like they did the season prior during this stretch from late-November to late-February, as goals came in bunches and the offense was backed up by strong goaltending from the tandem of Luongo and backup goaltender [[Cory Schneider]]. The peak of the Canucks' season came on January 7, 2012, in the 42nd game of the season which came against the [[Boston Bruins]], a rematch of the [[2011 Stanley Cup Finals]]. The Canucks prevailed 4–3 in a fight-filled game with a hard-fought playoff atmosphere, and they seemed to state to the hockey world that they would be heard from again come playoff time if they were to meet in the Stanley Cup Finals again. Despite their continuation of winning lengthy stretches of games within the last several weeks from early-March to early-April, the team did not play with the same heart they played with earlier in the season as they often played down to their competition by barely beating some of the weakest teams in the league and even lost games they had little business losing as the offense seemed to disappear and the team was lucky to have maintained outstanding goaltending and defense that kept them in games and eventually leading them to their second consecutive [[Presidents' Trophy]] and second Presidents' Trophy in franchise history altogether on the final day of the season on April 7, when they defeated the Edmonton Oilers 3–0 and the top seeded Eastern Conference team [[New York Rangers]] lost their season finale the same day 4–1 against the [[Washington Capitals]], ending their [[2011–12 New York Rangers season|season]] with 109 points in the standings, two points behind the Canucks 111 points. Despite entering the [[2012 Stanley Cup playoffs|2012 playoffs]] as the top seed in the Western Conference for the second year in a row and the back-to-back Presidents' Trophy winners, the Canucks were upset in the first round in five games by the eight-seeded [[Los Angeles Kings]], who would eventually go on to win their first Stanley Cup in franchise history as the weeks went on, making them the first, and so far only team to do so. This marked the third consecutive season and fourth time in six seasons where the Canucks lost a playoff series to an eventual Stanley Cup champion. {{TOClimit|limit=3}} ==Off-season== ===NHL entry draft=== [[File:Nicklas Jensen 2011 NHL Draft.jpg|thumb|right|Nicklas Jensen on stage after being selected 29th overall in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft|250px]] {{main|2011 NHL Entry Draft}} The [[2011 NHL entry draft]] was held June 24–25, 2011, at the [[Xcel Energy Center]] in [[Saint Paul, Minnesota]]. The Canucks selected eight players including [[Nicklas Jensen]] with their first-round draft choice, 29th overall. On day two of the entry draft the Vancouver Canucks traded their second-round draft choice to the [[Minnesota Wild]] for two picks in later rounds. In total, Vancouver selected eight players including [[David Honzík]], [[Alexandre Grenier]], [[Joseph LaBate]], [[Ludwig Blomstrand]], [[Frank Corrado]], Pathrik Westerholm and [[Henrik Tömmernes|Henrik Tommernes]]. In total, none would become regular NHL players, with Corrado playing the most games with 76 appearances across three teams. ===Minor League affiliations=== On June 21, 2011, True North Sports & Entertainment, the owners of the [[Manitoba Moose]] received Board of Governors approval to purchase and re-locate the [[Atlanta Thrashers]]. The Thrashers moved to [[Winnipeg]], Manitoba to replace the Manitoba Moose. The Moose announced that they were moving to St. John's and would become the [[American Hockey League|AHL]] affiliate of the [[Winnipeg Jets]]. As a result, the Canucks were left without an affiliate temporarily. On June 27, 2011, the Vancouver Canucks signed a two-year affiliation agreement with the [[Chicago Wolves]].{{cite web|title=Vancouver Canucks and Chicago Wolves announce new AHL affiliate RG Properties, who also owned the Victoria Salmon Kings, opted to fold the Salmon Kings franchise at the conclusion of the [[2010–11 ECHL season]].{{cite web|last=Dheensaw|first=Cleve|title=RG opts to fold Salmon Kings franchis|url=http://www.timescolonist.com/sports/opts+fold+Salmon+Kings+franchise/4744719/story.html|publisher=Times Colonist|accessdate=May 17, 2011|date=May 7, 2011}}{{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} As a result, the Canucks were left without an [[ECHL]] minor league affiliate. The Salmon Kings spent five years as the ECHL affiliate of the Vancouver Canucks. On September 22, the Vancouver Canucks announced that it had signed an ECHL affiliation agreement with the [[Kalamazoo Wings]].{{cite web|title=Vancouver Canucks and Kalamazoo Wings agree to new ECHL affiliate deal|url=https://canucks.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=589236|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110924024322/http://canucks.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=589236|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 24, 2011|publisher=[[Vancouver Canucks]]|accessdate=September 22, 2011|date=September 22, 2011}} ==Preseason== Training camp began for the rookies on September 9 and included two days of on-ice training sessions followed by a four-game Young Stars tournament featuring prospects from other teams including the [[Calgary Flames]], [[Edmonton Oilers]], [[San Jose Sharks]] and [[Winnipeg Jets]]. Among the players were four that were selected from the 2011 Entry Draft. Nicklas Jensen, David Honzik, Alexandre Grenier and Frank Corrado all took part in the Canucks rookie training camp and Young Stars tournament. LaBate did not participate in the camp because his college semester had begun while Blomstrand, Westerholm and Tommernes were in the midst of training camp for their own Swedish hockey clubs. The Vancouver Canucks main training camp started on September 16. Several veteran NHL players were invited to the camp on a try-out basis. These players included [[Owen Nolan]], [[Anders Eriksson (ice hockey b. 1975)|Anders Eriksson]], [[Niko Dimitrakos]] and [[Todd Fedoruk]]. However, none of the invites were able to secure a contract with the club. The Canucks played a total of eight preseason games where they finished with a record of 3–5. Much of the Vancouver Canucks roster were returning members from the 2010–11 season with the exception of [[Christian Ehrhoff]] and [[Raffi Torres]], who both changed teams, through trade and free agency respectively, during the off-season. Citing the shortened off-season due to their appearance in the [[2011 Stanley Cup Finals|Stanley Cup Finals]], the Vancouver Canucks management and coaching staff decided to give a majority of the veterans rest. As a result, players guaranteed roster spots in the regular season, such as [[Daniel Sedin|Daniel]] and [[Henrik Sedin]] only played in two preseason games. ==Regular season== Like [[2010–11 Vancouver Canucks season|2010–11]], the Canucks were met with extremely high expectations for the upcoming season. They entered 2011–12 as the defending [[Presidents' Trophy]] and [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] champions. It was a record setting season that saw them rank first in the league in goals per game, goals against per game and power play percentage. Both [[Roberto Luongo]] and [[Cory Schneider]] were awarded the [[William M. Jennings Trophy]] for lowest goals against. General consensus through various sports media outlets such as [[The Hockey News]], [[Sports Illustrated]], [[The Sports Network|TSN]] and [[Sportsnet]] predicted that the Canucks would return to the Western Conference Finals or at least finish first in the Western Conference regular season.{{cite web|title=The Hockey News 2011–12 NHL predictions|url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/the-hockey-news-2011-12-nhl-predictions|publisher=[[The Hockey News]]|access-date=October 16, 2011|date=September 4, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120405062721/http://www.thehockeynews.com/articles/41527-The-Hockey-News-201112-NHL-predictions.html|archive-date=April 5, 2012|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}}{{cite web|last=Dater|first=Adrian|title=2011–12 Northwest Div. Preview|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/adrian_dater/09/22/northwest.division.preview/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008012615/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/adrian_dater/09/22/northwest.division.preview/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 8, 2011|work=Sports Illustrated|accessdate=October 16, 2011|date=October 5, 2011}} ===October–November=== [[File:37 RYP Patch.svg|thumb|right|Helmet decal worn by the Vancouver Canucks team throughout the season|175px]] The Vancouver Canucks began their season on October 6 when they hosted the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] before embarking on a four-game road trip. Prior to the start of the home opener the Canucks organization held a ceremony to celebrate their [[2010–11 Vancouver Canucks season|2010–11 season]] and to thank the police officers, [[Firefighter|firemen]] and volunteers who helped the city recover after the [[2011 Vancouver Stanley Cup riot|Stanley Cup riot]]. The game was supposed to be [[Sidney Crosby]]'s third NHL game at [[Rogers Arena]], and first hockey game since scoring the [[Golden goal#Ice hockey|golden goal]] at the [[Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2010 Winter Olympics]] but was unable to play as he was still recovering from a [[concussion]]. In the game, the Vancouver Canucks battled back from a 3–1 deficit but fell short in a shootout. The club held a ceremony on October 18 prior to their game against the [[New York Rangers]] to honour the late [[Rick Rypien]]. Rypien played within the Vancouver Canucks organization for seven seasons, splitting time between the Canucks and the [[Manitoba Moose]], before signing with the [[Winnipeg Jets]] during the summer. Rypien was found dead at his home in [[Crowsnest Pass, Alberta]], on August 15. The Canucks wore a helmet decal in honour of Rypien during the season.{{cite web|last=Kuzma|first=Ben|title=Canucks will honour memory of Rypien with decal tribute, Oct. 18 ceremony|url=http://blogs.theprovince.com/2011/10/04/canucks-will-honour-memory-of-rypien-with-decal-tribute-oct-18-ceremony/|publisher=The White Towel|accessdate=October 6, 2011|date=October 3, 2011}} The Canucks also ran a video tribute for former Ranger [[Derek Boogaard]] who also died during the off-season.{{cite web|title=Derek Boogaard passes away at age 28|url=https://rangers.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=562775|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110518022732/http://rangers.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=562775|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 18, 2011|publisher=[[New York Rangers]]|accessdate=October 16, 2011|date=May 13, 2011}} The Canucks struggled throughout the month of October which was punctuated by a significant trade. Mikael Samuelsson and [[Marco Sturm]] were traded to the Florida Panthers on October 22, just hours after the Canucks defeated the [[Minnesota Wild]]. In return, the Canucks acquired a third-round draft pick in the [[2013 NHL entry draft]] and [[Forward (ice hockey)|forwards]] [[David Booth (ice hockey)|David Booth]] and [[Steven Reinprecht]]. The month ended with a match up against the [[Washington Capitals]] that saw the Canucks prevail by a final score of 7–4. [[Alexander Edler|Alex Edler]], Maxim Lapierre and [[Chris Higgins (ice hockey)|Chris Higgins]] all registered two goals for Vancouver while [[Alexander Ovechkin]] also scored a pair of goals for Washington. The month of November opened with a six-game road trip beginning in [[Calgary Flames|Calgary]], where the Canucks won the game by a score of 5–1. The game saw Daniel Sedin score his 254th goal of his career to tie [[Pavel Bure]] for fourth all-time in Canucks goal scoring. However, the Canucks continued to battle inconsistency and were unable to sustain any momentum through the first two-thirds of the month where they compiled a record of 4–4 capped by a blowout loss to rival [[Chicago Blackhawks|Chicago]]. The Canucks, led by [[Cory Schneider]] who originally replaced an injured [[Roberto Luongo]], finished the month with five consecutive victories that included back-to-back shutouts for Schneider. During the winning streak head coach [[Alain Vigneault]] became the team's winningest coach when the team defeated [[Colorado Avalanche|Colorado]] on November 23.{{cite news|title=Canucks 3, Avalanche 0|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/van-vs-col/2011/11/23/2011020310|agency=Associated Press|access-date=November 29, 2011|date=November 23, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111204171004/http://canucks.nhl.com/club/recap.htm?id=2011020310|archive-date=December 4, 2011|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} ==Standings== ===Divisional standings=== {{2011–12 NHL Northwest Division standings|team=VAN}} ===Conference standings=== {{2011–12 NHL Western Conference standings|team=VAN}} ==Schedule and results== ===Pre-season=== {| class="toccolours collapsible collapsed" style="width:90%; clear:both; margin:1.5em auto; text-align:center;" |- ! colspan=10 style="background:#003e7e; color:#c9c0bb;" | 2011 pre-season game log: 3–5–0 (Home: 2–2–0; Road: 1–3–0) |- style="text-align:center; background:#ddd;" ! # !! [[Kalamazoo Wings]] ([[ECHL]]) | GoalsLeader = [[Daniel Sedin]] (30) | AssistsLeader = [[Henrik Sedin]] (67) | PointsLeader = Henrik Sedin (81) | PIMLeader = [[Maxim Lapierre]] (130) | PlusMinusLeader = [[Dan Hamhuis]] (+29) | WinsLeader = [[Roberto Luongo]] (31) | GAALeader = [[Cory Schneider]] (1.96) | StanleyCup= | PresidentsTrophy= yes | ConferenceWin= | DivisionWin=yes }} The '''2011–12 Vancouver Canucks season''' was the 42nd season in the modern Canucks history. The [[Vancouver Canucks]] were the defending [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] champions and three time defending [[Northwest Division (NHL)|Northwest Division]] champions. The Canucks opened the regular season against the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] at home on October 6, 2011. Their final regular season game was held at [[Rogers Arena]] against the [[Edmonton Oilers]] on April 7, 2012. The Canucks entered the season expected to again contend for their first ever [[Stanley Cup]] after coming one win short from winning it the [[2010–11 Vancouver Canucks season|previous season]] and maintaining the majority of the players from the previous season on the roster. The Canucks struggled out of the gate, hovering around .500 until roughly the 20-game mark due to weak defensive play and a slow start from starting goaltender [[Roberto Luongo]]. The Canucks then recovered by the 20th game on November 20 against the [[Ottawa Senators]] (where they defeated the Senators 2–1) and would go on to play their best hockey of the season from that day until the end of February. The team dominated much like they did the season prior during this stretch from late-November to late-February, as goals came in bunches and the offense was backed up by strong goaltending from the tandem of Luongo and backup goaltender [[Cory Schneider]]. The peak of the Canucks' season came on January 7, 2012, in the 42nd game of the season which came against the [[Boston Bruins]], a rematch of the [[2011 Stanley Cup Finals]]. The Canucks prevailed 4–3 in a fight-filled game with a hard-fought playoff atmosphere, and they seemed to state to the hockey world that they would be heard from again come playoff time if they were to meet in the Stanley Cup Finals again. Despite their continuation of winning lengthy stretches of games within the last several weeks from early-March to early-April, the team did not play with the same heart they played with earlier in the season as they often played down to their competition by barely beating some of the weakest teams in the league and even lost games they had little business losing as the offense seemed to disappear and the team was lucky to have maintained outstanding goaltending and defense that kept them in games and eventually leading them to their second consecutive [[Presidents' Trophy]] and second Presidents' Trophy in franchise history altogether on the final day of the season on April 7, when they defeated the Edmonton Oilers 3–0 and the top seeded Eastern Conference team [[New York Rangers]] lost their season finale the same day 4–1 against the [[Washington Capitals]], ending their [[2011–12 New York Rangers season|season]] with 109 points in the standings, two points behind the Canucks 111 points. Despite entering the [[2012 Stanley Cup playoffs|2012 playoffs]] as the top seed in the Western Conference for the second year in a row and the back-to-back Presidents' Trophy winners, the Canucks were upset in the first round in five games by the eight-seeded [[Los Angeles Kings]], who would eventually go on to win their first Stanley Cup in franchise history as the weeks went on, making them the first, and so far only team to do so. This marked the third consecutive season and fourth time in six seasons where the Canucks lost a playoff series to an eventual Stanley Cup champion. {{TOClimit|limit=3}} ==Off-season== ===NHL entry draft=== [[File:Nicklas Jensen 2011 NHL Draft.jpg|thumb|right|Nicklas Jensen on stage after being selected 29th overall in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft|250px]] {{main|2011 NHL Entry Draft}} The [[2011 NHL entry draft]] was held June 24–25, 2011, at the [[Xcel Energy Center]] in [[Saint Paul, Minnesota]]. The Canucks selected eight players including [[Nicklas Jensen]] with their first-round draft choice, 29th overall. On day two of the entry draft the Vancouver Canucks traded their second-round draft choice to the [[Minnesota Wild]] for two picks in later rounds. In total, Vancouver selected eight players including [[David Honzík]], [[Alexandre Grenier]], [[Joseph LaBate]], [[Ludwig Blomstrand]], [[Frank Corrado]], Pathrik Westerholm and [[Henrik Tömmernes|Henrik Tommernes]]. In total, none would become regular NHL players, with Corrado playing the most games with 76 appearances across three teams. ===Minor League affiliations=== On June 21, 2011, True North Sports & Entertainment, the owners of the [[Manitoba Moose]] received Board of Governors approval to purchase and re-locate the [[Atlanta Thrashers]]. The Thrashers moved to [[Winnipeg]], Manitoba to replace the Manitoba Moose. The Moose announced that they were moving to St. John's and would become the [[American Hockey League|AHL]] affiliate of the [[Winnipeg Jets]]. As a result, the Canucks were left without an affiliate temporarily. On June 27, 2011, the Vancouver Canucks signed a two-year affiliation agreement with the [[Chicago Wolves]].{{cite web|title=Vancouver Canucks and Chicago Wolves announce new AHL affiliate agreement|url=https://canucks.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=567422|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629003000/http://canucks.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=567422|url-status=dead|archive-date=June [[Victoria Royals]] replaced the [[Victoria Salmon Kings]] and began play in the [[2011–12 WHL season]]. RG Properties, who also owned the Victoria Salmon Kings, opted to fold the Salmon Kings franchise at the conclusion of the [[2010–11 ECHL season]].{{cite web|last=Dheensaw|first=Cleve|title=RG opts to fold Salmon Kings franchis|url=http://www.timescolonist.com/sports/opts+fold+Salmon+Kings+franchise/4744719/story.html|publisher=Times Colonist|accessdate=May 17, 2011|date=May 7, 2011}}{{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} As a result, the Canucks were left without an [[ECHL]] minor league affiliate. The Salmon Kings spent five years as the ECHL affiliate of the Vancouver Canucks. On September 22, the Vancouver Canucks announced that it had signed an ECHL affiliation agreement with the [[Kalamazoo Wings]].{{cite web|title=Vancouver Canucks and Kalamazoo Wings agree to new ECHL affiliate deal|url=https://canucks.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=589236|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110924024322/http://canucks.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=589236|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 24, 2011|publisher=[[Vancouver Canucks]]|accessdate=September 22, 2011|date=September 22, 2011}} ==Preseason== Training camp began for the rookies on September 9 and included two days of on-ice training sessions followed by a four-game Young Stars tournament featuring prospects from other teams including the [[Calgary Flames]], [[Edmonton Oilers]], [[San Jose Sharks]] and [[Winnipeg Jets]]. Among the players were four that were selected from the 2011 Entry Draft. Nicklas Jensen, David Honzik, Alexandre Grenier and Frank Corrado all took part in the Canucks rookie training camp and Young Stars tournament. LaBate did not participate in the camp because his college semester had begun while Blomstrand, Westerholm and Tommernes were in the midst of training camp for their own Swedish hockey clubs. The Vancouver Canucks main training camp started on September 16. Several veteran NHL players were invited to the camp on a try-out basis. These players included [[Owen Nolan]], [[Anders Eriksson (ice hockey b. 1975)|Anders Eriksson]], [[Niko Dimitrakos]] and [[Todd Fedoruk]]. However, none of the invites were able to secure a contract with the club. The Canucks played a total of eight preseason games where they finished with a record of 3–5. Much of the Vancouver Canucks roster were returning members from the 2010–11 season with the exception of [[Christian Ehrhoff]] and [[Raffi Torres]], who both changed teams, through trade and free agency respectively, during the off-season. Citing the shortened off-season due to their appearance in the [[2011 Stanley Cup Finals|Stanley Cup Finals]], the Vancouver Canucks management and coaching staff decided to give a majority of the veterans rest. As a result, players guaranteed roster spots in the regular season, such as [[Daniel Sedin|Daniel]] and [[Henrik Sedin]] only played in two preseason games. ==Regular season== Like [[2010–11 Vancouver Canucks season|2010–11]], the Canucks were met with extremely high expectations for the upcoming season. They entered 2011–12 as the defending [[Presidents' Trophy]] and [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] champions. It was a record setting season that saw them rank first in the league in goals per game, goals against per game and power play percentage. Both [[Roberto Luongo]] and [[Cory Schneider]] were awarded the [[William M. Jennings Trophy]] for lowest goals against. General consensus through various sports media outlets such as [[The Hockey News]], [[Sports Illustrated]], [[The Sports Network|TSN]] and [[Sportsnet]] predicted that the Canucks would return to the Western Conference Finals or at least finish first in the Western Conference regular season.{{cite web|title=The Hockey News 2011–12 NHL predictions|url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/the-hockey-news-2011-12-nhl-predictions|publisher=[[The Hockey News]]|access-date=October 16, 2011|date=September 4, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120405062721/http://www.thehockeynews.com/articles/41527-The-Hockey-News-201112-NHL-predictions.html|archive-date=April 5, 2012|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}}{{cite web|last=Dater|first=Adrian|title=2011–12 Northwest Div. Preview|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/adrian_dater/09/22/northwest.division.preview/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008012615/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/adrian_dater/09/22/northwest.division.preview/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 8, 2011|work=Sports Illustrated|accessdate=October 16, 2011|date=October 5, 2011}} ===October–November=== [[File:37 RYP Patch.svg|thumb|right|Helmet decal worn by the Vancouver Canucks team throughout the season|175px]] The Vancouver Canucks began their season on October 6 when they hosted the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] before embarking on a four-game road trip. Prior to the start of the home opener the Canucks organization held a ceremony to celebrate their [[2010–11 Vancouver Canucks season|2010–11 season]] and to thank the police officers, [[Firefighter|firemen]] and volunteers who helped the city recover after the [[2011 Vancouver Stanley Cup riot|Stanley Cup riot]]. The game was supposed to be [[Sidney Crosby]]'s third NHL game at [[Rogers Arena]], and first hockey game since scoring the [[Golden goal#Ice hockey|golden goal]] at the [[Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2010 Winter Olympics]] but was unable to play as he was still recovering from a [[concussion]]. In the game, the Vancouver Canucks battled back from a 3–1 deficit but fell short in a shootout. The club held a ceremony on October 18 prior to their game against the [[New York Rangers]] to honour the late [[Rick Rypien]]. Rypien played within the Vancouver Canucks organization for seven seasons, splitting time between the Canucks and the [[Manitoba Moose]], before signing with the [[Winnipeg Jets]] during the summer. Rypien was found dead at his home in [[Crowsnest Pass, Alberta]], on August 15. The Canucks wore a helmet decal in honour of Rypien during the season.{{cite web|last=Kuzma|first=Ben|title=Canucks will honour memory of Rypien with decal tribute, Oct. 18 ceremony|url=http://blogs.theprovince.com/2011/10/04/canucks-will-honour-memory-of-rypien-with-decal-tribute-oct-18-ceremony/|publisher=The White Towel|accessdate=October 6, 2011|date=October 3, 2011}} The Canucks also ran a video tribute for former Ranger [[Derek Boogaard]] who also died during the off-season.{{cite web|title=Derek Boogaard passes away at age 28|url=https://rangers.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=562775|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110518022732/http://rangers.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=562775|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 18, 2011|publisher=[[New York Rangers]]|accessdate=October 16, 2011|date=May 13, 2011}} The Canucks struggled throughout the month of October which was punctuated by a significant trade. Mikael Samuelsson and [[Marco Sturm]] were traded to the Florida Panthers on October 22, just hours after the Canucks defeated the [[Minnesota Wild]]. In return, the Canucks acquired a third-round draft pick in the [[2013 NHL entry draft]] and [[Forward (ice hockey)|forwards]] [[David Booth (ice hockey)|David Booth]] and [[Steven Reinprecht]]. The month ended with a match up against the [[Washington Capitals]] that saw the Canucks prevail by a final score of 7–4. [[Alexander Edler|Alex Edler]], Maxim Lapierre and [[Chris Higgins (ice hockey)|Chris Higgins]] all registered two goals for Vancouver while [[Alexander Ovechkin]] also scored a pair of goals for Washington. The month of November opened with a six-game road trip beginning in [[Calgary Flames|Calgary]], where the Canucks won the game by a score of 5–1. The game saw Daniel Sedin score his 254th goal of his career to tie [[Pavel Bure]] for fourth all-time in Canucks goal scoring. However, the Canucks continued to battle inconsistency and were unable to sustain any momentum through the first two-thirds of the month where they compiled a record of 4–4 capped by a blowout loss to rival [[Chicago Blackhawks|Chicago]]. The Canucks, led by [[Cory Schneider]] who originally replaced an injured [[Roberto Luongo]], finished the month with five consecutive victories that included back-to-back shutouts for Schneider. During the winning streak head coach [[Alain Vigneault]] became the team's winningest coach when the team defeated [[Colorado Avalanche|Colorado]] on November 23.{{cite news|title=Canucks 3, Avalanche 0|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/van-vs-col/2011/11/23/2011020310|agency=Associated Press|access-date=November 29, 2011|date=November 23, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111204171004/http://canucks.nhl.com/club/recap.htm?id=2011020310|archive-date=December 4, 2011|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} ==Standings== ===Divisional standings=== {{2011–12 NHL Northwest Division standings|team=VAN}} ===Conference standings=== {{2011–12 NHL Western Conference standings|team=VAN}} ==Schedule and results== ===Pre-season=== {| class="toccolours collapsible collapsed" style="width:90%; clear:both; margin:1.5em auto; text-align:center;" |- ! colspan=10 style="background:#003e7e; color:#c9c0bb;" | 2011 pre-season game log: 3–5–0 (Home: 2–2–0; Road: 1–3–0) |- style="text-align:center; background:#ddd;" ! # !!
