Weber was also seen as a possible [power play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_play_(sporting_term) "Power play (sporting term)") contributor as a right-handed defenceman with a hard shot, potentially playing a role similar to that of former Canuck [Sami Salo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Salo "Sami Salo").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-19) Santorelli was not expected to make the team initially, but would add depth to the Canucks new [American Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League") (AHL) affiliate, the [Utica Comets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utica_Comets "Utica Comets") instead.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-santo-20)

### Training camp

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Training camp")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Lack_and_Luongo.jpg/250px-Lack_and_Luongo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lack_and_Luongo.jpg)

[Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo") and [Eddie Lack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_L%C3%A4ck "Eddie Läck") (right)

At the start of training camp Tortorella promised to make changes to the way the Canucks played. He wanted to make the team tougher to play against.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-21) Some of the techniques he felt would accomplish this were hard [forechecking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forecheck "Forecheck"), protecting the puck, being strong along the boards, and increasing shot blocking.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-22) The Canucks finished the 2012–13 season as the 27th ranked team in blocked shots while the Rangers finished sixth.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-23) Tortorella also said that he would use the Sedin twins to [kill penalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kill "Penalty kill"). The Sedins had asked Vigneault to be used on the penalty kill, but he opted to keep them rested for their offensive role instead. Upon learning that they would be killing penalties [Henrik Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin") said: "It's something that I think is a big part of becoming a great player. You have to be on the ice for all situations. For us, we were counted upon to score goals, and if we didn't, then we were terrible. I think you grow as players when you play all situations."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-24) Tortorella put the Canucks through a physically demanding training camp.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-tough-25) Players were asked to run two miles in 12 minutes and were put through a series of intense skating drills.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-tough-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-26) Tortorella believed he could learn about his players when they were exhausted and asked them to give a little more.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-tough-25)

For the second consecutive year, goaltending was a focus of training camp. After choosing to keep Luongo, the team did not hear from him. He had fired his longtime agent, and hired new representation.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-battle-27) This development set off speculation that Luongo would not report to training camp and would try to force a trade.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-battle-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-28) Shortly after the change in representation, his new agents announced that Luongo would attend training camp.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-29) In his first interview following the Schneider trade, Luongo stated that he had looked into voiding his contract, but he planned to honor it, and wanted to re-establish himself as an elite goaltender.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-30)

The Canucks had two competitors for the back-up goaltender position, [Eddie Lack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_L%C3%A4ck "Eddie Läck") and [Joacim Eriksson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joacim_Eriksson "Joacim Eriksson").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-31) Lack had been seen as the heir apparent for the back-up role, but following a season-ending injury after playing only 12 games in the AHL, his future was called into question.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-32) Eriksson was signed to a two-year, [two-way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-way_contract "Two-way contract"), entry-level contract with the Canucks in the off-season after helping [Skellefteå AIK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skellefte%C3%A5_AIK "Skellefteå AIK") to the [Swedish Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Hockey_League "Swedish Hockey League") championship.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-34) Though neither player had any NHL experience, Lack was seen as the front runner because of his [one-way contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockey_contracts#One-way_contract "Hockey contracts"), which paid him the same at the NHL or AHL level.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-35)

## Preseason

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Preseason")]

At the start of preseason, Vancouver hoped to add six young rookies to the team. While the goaltending situation almost assured that one rookie would be added, forwards [Hunter Shinkaruk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_Shinkaruk "Hunter Shinkaruk"), [Brendan Gaunce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Gaunce "Brendan Gaunce"), [Nicklas Jensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicklas_Jensen "Nicklas Jensen"), and Horvat were also attempting to make the team. Defenceman [Frank Corrado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Corrado "Frank Corrado") was looking to secure a regular spot after he played the final three regular season, and four playoff games for the Canucks in 2012–13.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-waiting-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-37) When asked about adding youngsters to the line-up Tortorella stated: "We're not going to force it, but we need to get some kids in our lineup."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-38) In Vancouver's first preseason game Shinkaruk and Gaunce scored goals, while Lack stopped 25 of 27 shots in two periods of work. Vancouver lost the game 3–2 to San Jose as the Sharks out shot the Canucks 42–15.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-39)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/Zack_Kassian_Canucks_practice_2012c.jpg/250px-Zack_Kassian_Canucks_practice_2012c.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zack_Kassian_Canucks_practice_2012c.jpg)

[Zack Kassian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Kassian "Zack Kassian") received an eight-game suspension for the reckless use of his stick.

Two games later, they played the [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton_Oilers "Edmonton Oilers"). [Winger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winger_(ice_hockey) "Winger (ice hockey)")[David Booth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Booth_(ice_hockey) "David Booth (ice hockey)") was scheduled to return to the line-up for the first time since an ankle injury ended his previous season in March. During the morning practice he suffered a groin injury but returned for the game.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-40)[Jordan Schroeder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Schroeder "Jordan Schroeder") became the first casualty of shot blocking suffering a [hairline fracture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hairline_fracture "Hairline fracture") in his foot after being struck by a [Nail Yakupov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_Yakupov "Nail Yakupov") shot.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-pile-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-ebner-42) Jensen was checked hard into the boards and sustained a shoulder injury.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-43)[Dale Weise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_Weise "Dale Weise") delivered a check to [Taylor Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Hall "Taylor Hall") striking the Oilers' forward in the head. Hall later said that the hit was "probably a mistake on both parts" and "I have to have my head up". Hall was uninjured on the play and stayed in the game. The hit was reviewed by the NHL's Senior Vice President, and disciplinarian, [Brendan Shanahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Shanahan "Brendan Shanahan") who suspended Weise for the remaining three games of the preseason.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-stickswing-45) Later in the game [Zack Kassian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Kassian "Zack Kassian") attempted to deliver a [body check](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checking_(ice_hockey) "Checking (ice hockey)") to [Sam Gagner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Gagner "Sam Gagner"), who made a hard stop to avoid contact.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-46) Kassian began a spin move while swinging his stick towards Gagner,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-fivegames-47) lost his balance so that it hit Gagner's head. He suffered a broken jaw, eventually missing the first 13 games of the season. Kassian was assessed a double minor penalty for high sticking.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-48) In a post game interview, Oilers head coach [Dallas Eakins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Eakins "Dallas Eakins") called the action "a disturbing play by a disturbing player".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-stickswing-45) During his disciplinary review of the play, Shanahan said that he accepted Kassian's claim that he did not intend to strike Gagner in the head, but that he was responsible for his actions. He suspended Kassian for eight games – the remaining three pre-season, and five regular season games.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-fivegames-47)

With one week remaining in the pre-season, Vancouver assigned Eriksson to the Comets, giving Lack the back-up goaltender job. Eriksson made only one appearance in the preseason and stopped all nine shots. The move was seen as a way for Eriksson to have more playing time while adjusting to the smaller ice surface in [North American rinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey_rink "Ice hockey rink").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-49) In the battle for the sixth defenceman spot, Alberts struggled in the preseason. In four games he registered 17 minutes in penalties, and was on the ice for eight goals against.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-lostjob-50) Weber was inconsistent. In his first, third, and fifth games he combined for one goal and three assists, with a [+4 rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plus%E2%80%93minus_(sports) "Plus–minus (sports)") (positive impact), while in his second and fourth games he recorded 1 assist and a −4 rating (negative impact).[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-55) The duo struggled in the second to last preseason game against San Jose, combining for a −6 rating.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-56) Though Corrado had played well enough to be considered among the team's top eight defencemen, he was assigned to Utica to allow him more, varied ice time to help his development.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-57)

Just prior to the Canucks' 23-man roster being set following the end of preseason, they claimed defenceman [Ryan Stanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Stanton_(ice_hockey,_born_1989) "Ryan Stanton (ice hockey, born 1989)") off [waivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waivers_(NHL) "Waivers (NHL)").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-stanton-58) Stanton had played only one NHL game but was brought in as a possible replacement for Alberts in order to keep a balance between right and left handed defencemen.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-lostjob-50) The youth movement failed to take hold.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-waiting-36) Guance was sent back to the [Belleville Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belleville_Bulls "Belleville Bulls"). Despite having a good camp, he was outplayed by fellow prospects, Horvat and Shinkaruk. Tortorella felt Gaunce needed to improve the tempo and the pace of his game and he would benefit from playing more minutes.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-59) Due to the injuries and suspensions, it appeared that Horvat and Shinkaruk would start the season with the Canucks.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-60) However, just days before the roster was set, Vancouver acquired forwards [Zac Dalpe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zac_Dalpe "Zac Dalpe") and [Jeremy Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Welsh "Jeremy Welsh") from the [Carolina Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Hurricanes "Carolina Hurricanes").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-61) Following the trade Horvat was sent back to the [London Knights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Knights "London Knights"), Shinkaruk remained with the team, but was returned to the [Medicine Hat Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine_Hat_Tigers "Medicine Hat Tigers") to make room for Stanton.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-stanton-58)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-62) As with the rest of the prospects, Vancouver was pleased with their play, but wanted to do what was best for their development.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-63) Helping to make the decision to return the prospects to their junior teams was the emergence of Mike Santorelli who had a strong camp, where he was one of Vancouver's best forwards.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-65) He earned Tortorella's trust and was played in all situations helping him to make the team.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-66)

## Regular season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Regular season")]

### October

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: October")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Mike_Santorelli_10-17-2013.jpg/250px-Mike_Santorelli_10-17-2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mike_Santorelli_10-17-2013.jpg)

[Mike Santorelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Santorelli "Mike Santorelli") scored back to back game winners in October.

Vancouver opened the season in San Jose. [Jason Garrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Garrison "Jason Garrison"), a member of the [top power play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_play_(sporting_term) "Power play (sporting term)") unit, scored a goal to give the Canucks the lead. Vancouver eventually lost 4–1. Having Garrison play with the top unit was seen as a change in philosophy from the previous season.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-opener-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-clippings-68) He was originally brought in to help with the Cauncks inconsistent power play, however he was played sparingly with the top unit and the team finished 22nd of 30 in the League for power play percentage.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-clippings-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-69) During the game, [Alexandre Burrows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandre_Burrows "Alexandre Burrows") blocked a [slap shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slap_shot "Slap shot") on a [penalty kill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kill "Penalty kill"), and suffered a hairline fracture to his foot, forcing him to miss 12 games.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-ebner-42)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-70) The Canucks earned Tortorella his first win as head coach with a 6–2 victory over Edmonton in the second game of the season.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-71) Lack made his NHL debut in the third game against the [Calgary Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Calgary_Flames_season "2013–14 Calgary Flames season"). Tortorella altered his lines to get the team going, including splitting up [Henrik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin") and [Daniel Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Sedin "Daniel Sedin"), something rarely done by Vigneault. The Canucks eventually won the game 5–4 in overtime on a Santorelli goal. Despite giving up four goals, Lack earned praise for his performance.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-74)

Following the Calgary game, Vancouver faced off with the [New Jersey Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_New_Jersey_Devils_season "2013–14 New Jersey Devils season"). The game was the first match-up of Luongo versus Schneider.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-75) Both goaltenders tried to downplay it, though Schneider admitted he was trying to outplay Luongo.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-77) Vancouver won the game in overtime with a second straight, game-winning goal by Santorelli.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-78) Vancouver played San Jose on October 10, again losing 4–1. During the game [Alexander Edler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Edler "Alexander Edler") hit San Jose rookie [Tomas Hertl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A1%C5%A1_Hertl "Tomáš Hertl")'s head, knocking his helmet off.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-79) Hertl was not hurt, and no penalty was called on the play, but Edler was suspended for three games the following day for the hit. The NHL Department of Player Safety deemed the hit illegal, as the principle point of contact was with the head. The length of the suspension was increased because Edler was a repeat offender.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-80) Tortorella believed that the suspension caused Edler to be more tentative defensively for the rest of the season.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-81) Vancouver lost the next home game before starting a seven-game road trip, their longest of the season.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-82)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Canucks_Win.jpg/250px-Canucks_Win.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Canucks_Win.jpg)

Canucks players congratulate [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo") on his 63rd career shutout.

The Canucks were down in first game of the trip against the [Philadelphia Flyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Philadelphia_Flyers_season "2013–14 Philadelphia Flyers season"), when Tortorella split up the Sedin twins leading to a comeback win for Vancouver.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-fool-83) While the Canucks were finding ways to win, their power play produced only two goals in 20 opportunities. This left the team's power play ranked twenty-seventh of thirty following the game in Philadelphia.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-84) While the Sedin twins practiced on separate lines following successful stints apart from each other, ultimately second line centre [Ryan Kesler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Kesler "Ryan Kesler") was moved to right wing to join them on the top line.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-fool-83)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-excel-85) In their next game against the [Buffalo Sabres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Buffalo_Sabres_season "2013–14 Buffalo Sabres season"), Roberto Luongo made 25 saves helping Vancouver to a 3–0 win. It was Luongo's 63rd career [shutout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shutout_(ice_hockey) "Shutout (ice hockey)"), giving him sole possession of 15th place for all-time shutouts, breaking the tie with [Turk Broda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk_Broda "Turk Broda").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-86) The Canucks lost their next two games, before recording three straight wins finishing with a 5–1–1 record[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#endnote_note_1) – the most successful road trip in team history.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-global-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-88)

The winning streak moved the Canucks into a first place tie in the [Pacific Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Division_(NHL) "Pacific Division (NHL)") with San Jose.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-global-87)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-89) Kesler recorded six goals and three assists on the trip which helped him earn the [NHL's Third Star of the Week Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_2013%E2%80%9314_NHL_Three_Star_Awards "List of 2013–14 NHL Three Star Awards").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-excel-85)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-thirdstar-90) Vancouver split their final two games finishing the month with a 9–5–1 record, putting them in fourth place in the division, three points behind San Jose.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-91) Although the Canucks were competitive, concerns were raised that the lengthy amount of ice time Tortorella was giving his top players would wear them down as the season progressed. Kesler and the Sedin twins led the league in total ice time among forwards, but trailed [Sidney Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Crosby "Sidney Crosby") in terms of average ice time for forwards.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-92)

### November

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: November")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Pavel_Bure_1997.jpg/250px-Pavel_Bure_1997.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pavel_Bure_1997.jpg)

The Canucks retired [Pavel Bure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Bure "Pavel Bure")'s number 10 in November.

On the first day of November, Vancouver signed the Sedin twins to matching four-year $28.5 million contract extensions.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-93) Before the first game of the month on November, Vancouver honoured [Pavel Bure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Bure "Pavel Bure") by retiring his jersey number 10. He had played seven seasons in Vancouver, scoring 254 goals, including back-to-back 60-goal seasons. He won the [Calder Memorial Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calder_Memorial_Trophy "Calder Memorial Trophy") as NHL Rookie of the Year as a Canuck, and was an integral part of the team's [1994 Stanley Cup Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Stanley_Cup_Final "1994 Stanley Cup Final") run. In addition, the team also changed the name of one of its year end team awards from the Most Exciting Player Award to the [Pavel Bure Most Exciting Player Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavel_Bure_Most_Exciting_Player_Award "Pavel Bure Most Exciting Player Award"). Bure called it a "great night", adding: "It's probably the biggest honor you can get. I'm really pleased."[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-95)

Vancouver won the game 4–0, with their second goal coming on a power play, the fifth of the season. The power play continued to be a struggle with the Canucks ranked twenty-eight in the league.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-96) During the game, Burrows taunted [Maple Leafs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Maple_Leafs "Toronto Maple Leafs")' forward [Phil Kessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Kessel "Phil Kessel"), by making slashing motions with his stick – a reference to an altercation Kessel had with [John Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Scott_(ice_hockey,_born_1982) "John Scott (ice hockey, born 1982)") earlier in the season. This taunting led to a scuffle and both players received [major penalties for fighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighting_in_ice_hockey "Fighting in ice hockey").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-97) Leafs' forward [Dave Bolland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Bolland "Dave Bolland") was injured after a hit by Kassian. While finishing his check, Kassian's skate came off the ice, sliced Bolland's ankle, cutting a tendon. After the game, Kassian said that he felt it was a clean hit but added: "Obviously, people are going to talk especially with my suspension before. But there's nothing there". Toronto's general manager [Dave Nonis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Nonis "Dave Nonis") noted that the injury was accidental.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-98) Following the Toronto game, Vancouver set out on a four-game division road trip.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-99)

Before the first game against the [Phoenix Coyotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Phoenix_Coyotes_season "2013–14 Phoenix Coyotes season"), Vancouver made some personnel changes. Booth was assigned to Utica on a conditioning assignment to help strengthen his groin, and to get more ice time to help him get up to game speed. Dalpe was called up to replace Booth after his own conditioning stint.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-100) The power play set-up was changed to four forwards and one defenceman, raising questions about Tortorella's decision to use [Dan Hamhuis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Hamhuis "Dan Hamhuis") as the lone defenceman. Hamhuis was known more as a shutdown defender and did not have one of the Canucks more powerful shots from the point.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-cannon-101) Vancouver led before giving up the tying goal with just over a minute remaining. The game went to a [shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shootout_(ice_hockey) "Shootout (ice hockey)") where Phoenix took the lead; Henrik Sedin had a chance to tie, but lost control of the puck and did not register a shot. Sedin did however, extend his point streak to a career-long 12 games and Hamhuis scored a power play goal.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-cannon-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-102) With the power play conversion, the Canucks were still twenty-sixth in the league at 10.9 percent.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-cannon-101)

Two days later the Canucks defeated San Jose, breaking a nine-game losing streak with the Sharks.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-103) Vancouver lost the final two games of the trip with a combined 8–2 score. Henrik Sedin went scoreless in the final three games of the trip, posting a –5 rating, and was demoted to the second line.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-104) Returning home, the Canucks fared no better, losing five of six games and posting a 1–2–3 record.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-sched-105) In all five losses the Canucks were tied or leading the game in the third period.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-110) Before the team's November 28 game in Ottawa, Totarella challenged Luongo to make more saves at important times during the game to help Vancouver win. He also moved Kesler back to center after he had failed to score an [even strength goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(ice_hockey) "Goal (ice hockey)") in 12 games.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-111) During the game Daniel Sedin scored his 300th career goal becoming the third player in franchise history to reach this mark, behind [Markus Naslund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_N%C3%A4slund "Markus Näslund") and [Trevor Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Linden "Trevor Linden").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-DS300-112)

In the final game of the month Vancouver played the [New York Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_New_York_Rangers_season "2013–14 New York Rangers season") and former coach Alain Vigneault. Daniel Sedin said of the game: "I know our former coach is over there, but once you get into the game you're not going to think too much about it. He was with us for seven years and he meant a lot to this franchise, so it's going to be fun seeing him again but once the game gets going we want the two points, and so does he".[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-DS300-112) Tortorella stated: "I'm not going to lie, it's a little weird for me coming back, but once the game starts, it's about playing and trying to find a way to get a win".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-Kreider-113) The Canucks lost the game 5–2, finishing the month with 31 points, four points out of the final playoff spot.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-Kreider-113)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-114)

### December through February

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: December through February")]

During December, the team won seven straight games beginning with a 6–2 victory over the [Boston Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Boston_Bruins_season "2013–14 Boston Bruins season"). They finished the month with a 10–1–2 record. Starting goaltender Roberto Luongo was injured during a 2–1 victory over the [Winnipeg Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Winnipeg_Jets_season "2013–14 Winnipeg Jets season"). Eddie Lack was the starting goalie for the rest of December.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-115)

The team started to struggle in January after losing to the [Philadelphia Flyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Philadelphia_Flyers_season "2013–14 Philadelphia Flyers season") at the end of December. Luongo managed to recover from his injury and played in the game against the [Los Angeles Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Los_Angeles_Kings_season "2013–14 Los Angeles Kings season"). But he was injured again when [Dustin Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Brown_(ice_hockey) "Dustin Brown (ice hockey)") scored and crashed into him, and was unable to play for six games. Eddie Lack struggled, posting a 1–3–2 record. On January 15, the Canucks lost 9–1 to the [Anaheim Ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Anaheim_Ducks_season "2013–14 Anaheim Ducks season"), the worst scoring game of the season. Henrik Sedin was injured during the next game. On January 18, the Canucks played the [Calgary Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Calgary_Flames_season "2013–14 Calgary Flames season"), a game which featured a first period brawl. Between periods, John Tortorella attempted to enter the Flames' dressing room, an act that resulted in the NHL suspending him for 15 days.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-15Days-116) Bob Hartley, the Flames' coach, was fined over the incident.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-15Days-116) Mike Sullivan took over from Tortorella as coach, but the team posted a losing record of 2–4–0 for the rest of January.

Tortorella returned for the first game in February. The Canucks lost to the [Detroit Red Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Detroit_Red_Wings_season "2013–14 Detroit Red Wings season"). Subsequently, the team lost four straight games which result in a seven-game losing streak when combined with the last two games in January. This was the team's worst losing streak since the 1990s.

The Canucks ended their losing streak against the [St. Louis Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_St._Louis_Blues_season "2013–14 St. Louis Blues season"), but lost to the [Minnesota Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Minnesota_Wild_season "2013–14 Minnesota Wild season") a few days later. Eddie Lack started both games, posting a 1–0–1 record, which convinced John Tortorella to start him in the [2014 Heritage Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Heritage_Classic "2014 Heritage Classic").

### March

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: March")]

During the Heritage Classic game the Canucks led 2–0, but ultimately lost 4–2. When they were down 3–2, fans were chanting: "We Want Lu!" (Luongo).[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-Defends-117) During post-game interviews Tortorella said that it was his choice to play Lack.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-Defends-117) On March 4, Luongo was traded to the [Florida Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Florida_Panthers_season "2013–14 Florida Panthers season") in exchange for [Shawn Matthias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Matthias "Shawn Matthias") and [Jacob Markstrom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Markstr%C3%B6m "Jacob Markström").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-118) Lack started in goal for the rest of March. On March 10, Vancouver was leading the [New York Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_New_York_Islanders_season "2013–14 New York Islanders season") 3–0 after two periods. The Islanders then scored seven goals in the third period, leading to a 7–4 Vancouver loss. This was the Canucks' worst single period of play since one in 1999 against the Red Wings. On March 16, the Canucks faced Roberto Luongo and the Florida Panthers for the first time since he had been traded. The Canucks won 4–3 in a shoot out. With playoff hopes fading quickly near the end of March, Vancouver then posted a three-game winning streak between March 20 and March 26. The streak came to an end with a loss to the [Colorado Avalanche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Colorado_Avalanche_season "2013–14 Colorado Avalanche season"). Vancouver lost to the Anaheim Ducks in the last game of the month.

### April

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: April")]

On April 1, Alain Vigneault returned to Vancouver with the [New York Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_New_York_Rangers_season "2013–14 New York Rangers season"). The Rangers won 3–1, damaging the Canucks' playoff hopes. A few days later, Mike Gillis was interviewed on TSN 1040 radio. He said, "I am not sure I'll be back next season."[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-119) On April 7, in a game which saw the Ducks up 3–0 against the Canucks with three minutes remaining in the game, fans starting chanting "Fire Gillis". The loss officially ended Vancouver's five-year playoff streak. Gillis was fired the next day.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-120)[Trevor Linden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Linden "Trevor Linden"), a former Canucks winger, replaced Gillis as president of hockey operations, though the team still needed to find a new general manager. After 19-straight starts, Lack was replaced in goal by Jacob Markstrom for the final three games. On April 12, after a 5–2 loss to the [Edmonton Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Edmonton_Oilers_season "2013–14 Edmonton Oilers season"), [Ryan Smyth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Smyth "Ryan Smyth") announced his retirement. On the last day of the regular season, Daniel Sedin was hit by [Paul Byron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Byron "Paul Byron") and left the ice on a stretcher with minor injuries. The Canucks went on to win 5–1 over the Calgary Flames. The Canucks ended the 2013–14 season with a 36–35–11 record.

## Canucks players in the Olympics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Canucks players in the Olympics")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/Roberto_Luongo_Canada_2010a.jpg/250px-Roberto_Luongo_Canada_2010a.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Roberto_Luongo_Canada_2010a.jpg)

[Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo") won a gold medal for Canada in the [2010 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey_at_the_2010_Winter_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament") as Canada's starting goaltender.

The NHL took a two-week break to allow players to play for their countries' teams in the [ice hockey event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey_at_the_2014_Winter_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Ice hockey at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament") at the [2014 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics "2014 Winter Olympics") in [Sochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi "Sochi"), Russia.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-121) Eight Canucks represented their respective countries at the Olympics.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-124)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-125)

Ryan Kesler played for Team USA.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-126)[Yannick Weber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yannick_Weber "Yannick Weber") was named to [Team Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_men's_national_ice_hockey_team "Switzerland men's national ice hockey team"), one of eight NHL players on the Swiss national team.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-127) On December 7, 2014, both Canada and Sweden announced their teams. The Sedin twins and [Alexander Edler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Edler "Alexander Edler") were named to the [Swedish national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden_men's_national_ice_hockey_team "Sweden men's national ice hockey team").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-128) Later in the day Luongo and [Dan Hamhuis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Hamhuis "Dan Hamhuis") were named to [Team Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_men's_national_ice_hockey_team "Canada men's national ice hockey team").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-Ronalds-129) (Luongo had won a gold medal for Canada in the [2010 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey_at_the_2010_Winter_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament") as the starting goaltender.) An eighth member of the Canucks organization was named to an Olympic team as prospect [Ronalds Kenins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronalds_%C4%B6%C4%93ni%C5%86%C5%A1 "Ronalds Ķēniņš") joined the [Latvia national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia_men's_national_ice_hockey_team "Latvia men's national ice hockey team") after having a strong [Olympic qualifying tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey_at_the_2014_Winter_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_qualification "Ice hockey at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's qualification").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-Ronalds-129)

Team Canada won the gold medal game with a 3–0 victory over Team Sweden. Dan Hamhuis and Roberto Luongo returned to Vancouver with gold medals, while Alexander Edler and Daniel Sedin returned with silver medals.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Vancouver_Canucks_season#cite_note-130)

The **2013–14 Vancouver Canucks season** was the franchise's [44th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Vancouver_Canucks_seasons "List of Vancouver Canucks seasons") in the [National Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hockey_League "National Hockey League") (NHL). The Canucks missed the [Stanley Cup playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Cup_playoffs "Stanley Cup playoffs") for the first time since the [2007–08 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Vancouver_Canucks_season "2007–08 Vancouver Canucks season"), ending their five-year playoff streak. In addition, the team recorded its worst regular season since the [1999–2000 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Vancouver_Canucks_season "1999–2000 Vancouver Canucks season"). Head coach [John Tortorella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Tortorella "John Tortorella"), who had been hired in the pre-season, was fired.

In addition to hiring Tortorella in the off-season, for financial reasons the decision was made to retain goaltender [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo") instead of [Cory Schneider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cory_Schneider "Cory Schneider"). As a result, along with a reduced salary cap, the team was unable to pursue top [free agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_agent "Free agent") signing a number of restricted and unrestricted free agents instead.

The team had won their division five years in a row previously, and had finished first in the entire league twice in the last three seasons. With the addition of a new head coach, and players such as [Brad Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Richardson "Brad Richardson"), both management and fans were optimistic that the team could be a Stanley Cup contender.

The team was inconsistent, playing well in October and December, but badly in November. In January the team's situation worsened. Tortorella's bombastic approach began to wear on team members, and top performers like [Alex Burrows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Burrows "Alex Burrows"), [Daniel Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Sedin "Daniel Sedin") and [Henrik Sedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henrik_Sedin "Henrik Sedin") were failing to score goals. Things deteriorated as the year progressed. Goaltender Roberto Luongo became disgruntled with a lack of playing time and forced a trade in March, while the team continued to fall in the standings. General manager [Mike Gillis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Gillis "Mike Gillis") was fired in April. Vancouver ended the season finishing sixth last overall out of thirty teams. This finish allowed the team to select sixth overall at the [2014 Entry Draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NHL_Entry_Draft "2014 NHL Entry Draft"), the lowest the Canucks had selected since [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_NHL_Entry_Draft "1999 NHL Entry Draft") when the team selected second and third overall.
